stories.title: Janata Darshan cancelled tomorrow for plantation drive:CM urges everyone to plant a tree and take responsibility for its protection
stories.summary: The regular 'Janata Darshan' (public audience) held during Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's visit to Gorakhpur will not take place on Sunday (12 July). The decision to postpone it has been taken due to the 'Plantation Mahayagya 2026'. The state has a target of planting 35 crore saplings. To achieve this, the Chief Minister will inaugurate this grand plantation drive by planting a sapling near the Gorakhpur Link Expressway on Sunday at 7:45 AM. The Shri Gorakhnath Temple office has stated that the Janata Darshan programme will remain postponed tomorrow to ensure maximum public participation in this grand plantation drive. The Chief Minister will arrive at the Gorakhpur Link Expressway at 7:45 AM. There, he will plant a sapling near the Bhagwanpur Toll Plaza. With this, the 'Plantation Mahayagya' will commence across the entire state. After this, he will address the public meeting organised there. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has appealed to all state residents to ensure their participation in the tree plantation mega-campaign by planting at least one sapling and taking a pledge to protect it. The Chief Minister said that in line with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's call, every citizen should try to convert the resolve of environmental protection into a reality by planting 'one tree in the name of mother'. Complainants come from far and wide Upon receiving information about the Chief Minister's presence in Gorakhpur, complainants come from far and wide to Gorakhnath Temple with their problems. Usually, when the Chief Minister is present here, a 'Janata Darshan' (public audience) is organised. This is the first time that an official announcement has been issued regarding the postponement of the 'Janata Darshan' programme. The purpose behind issuing the information on time is to prevent people from coming here unnecessarily and facing inconvenience. The Chief Minister will depart for Lucknow tomorrow afternoon.

stories.title: Kali temple dome collapses during road widening work:PWD employee killed, another injured; demolition halted
stories.summary: A major accident occurred late on Friday night during the demolition of an ancient Kali temple in the Mughalsarai Kotwali area amid road widening work. During the demolition, the massive dome of the temple suddenly collapsed. A PWD employee died in the accident, while another person was seriously injured. The demolition work was underway late at night using a bulldozer for road widening. During this time, PWD employee Jhumri alias Baldev (58), a resident of Padav Dandi, was standing there holding a rope. Suddenly, the temple dome collapsed. While falling, the dome hit the bulldozer bucket, changed direction and fell on Baldev and another person, trapping them. Chaos broke out at the spot after the accident. Both injured persons were immediately taken to hospital, where Baldev died during treatment. The other injured person is undergoing treatment. After the incident, administrative officials, police personnel and local residents started relief and rescue operations. The demolition work was halted for some time as a safety measure. As soon as the information was received, Mughalsarai SDM Rajiv Mohan Saxena and Kotwali in-charge Vijay Pratap Singh reached the spot. The officials inspected the site and gathered details about the entire incident. The cause of the accident is being investigated.

stories.title: Bird hits Flydubai aircraft in Lucknow:Emergency landing carried out, 163 passengers onboard; plane stranded at airport for 6 hours
stories.summary: A Flydubai aircraft (FD-443) heading to Lucknow was hit by a bird on Saturday morning when it was approaching the city. Following the bird strike, the pilot carried out an emergency landing. The aircraft had 163 passengers onboard. The flight was scheduled to reach Lucknow at 6:35 am and was expected to arrive 40 minutes late. After the bird hit, the pilot requested an emergency slot on the runway. The aircraft landed safely at Lucknow airport at 7:13 am. Even after around six hours, the aircraft remained parked in the airport’s parking bay at 1:30 pm. Following the incident, the plane was moved from the runway to the parking bay, where a detailed technical inspection is being carried out. The aircraft was already delayed by 48 minutes from its scheduled time. The same aircraft was scheduled to depart from Lucknow for Dubai again after an hour.

stories.title: Advocate thrashes constable in Kanpur:Cop, who appeared drunk, suspended; FIR to be filed after probe
stories.summary: A video of an advocate allegedly beating a police constable near the Kanpur court went viral on social media on Friday. After receiving information about the incident, DCP East ordered an investigation. Following a preliminary probe, the constable involved in the dispute was suspended. A departmental inquiry has also been initiated. A case will be registered after the investigation report is submitted. Constable suspended ACP Line Anand Ojha said a video went viral on Friday evening showing a fight and argument between two police personnel and an advocate. During the investigation, it was found that one of the two constables seen in the video had already been suspended and had been absent for a long time. The other constable was immediately suspended on charges of indiscipline and inappropriate conduct. The preliminary investigation suggested that the constable appeared to be intoxicated. People present at the spot also claimed that the dispute occurred while the constable was under the influence of alcohol. Action was taken against the constable based on these findings. The matter is currently under investigation, and further action will be taken soon based on statements from both sides and available evidence.

stories.title: Nripendra Mishra calls Ram Mandir donation theft a stigma:SP poster says, 'Ram naam japna, chadhaya daan apna'
stories.summary: In the Ayodhya Ram Mandir donation theft case, Nripendra Mishra, chairman of the Ram Mandir Construction Committee, said on Saturday that the incident was “a kind of stigma”. He said that everyone involved was not only saddened by it but also felt “embarrassed”. “I have full faith that the system will be improved and such incidents will not happen again,” Mishra said. He added, “A high-level committee has been formed. A judge is likely to be its chairman. The committee will submit its decision and recommendations to the trust, which will then consider them.” Nripendra Mishra arrived at the Ram Katha Museum on Saturday to attend the second day of the Ram Temple Construction Committee meeting. Earlier, during the meeting held at the Ram Temple premises on Friday, none of the trust members had attended. Meanwhile, in Gorakhpur, Samajwadi Party leader Upendra Dutt Shukla put up posters on Friday night targeting the controversy. The posters read: “Chanting Ram’s name, claiming devotees’ donations. Lord Ram had told Sita that such an age would come, where thieves would steal from temples and the watchman would only watch.” In Raebareli, the Vishva Hindu Raksha Parishad (VHRP) national general secretary Rahul Singh hit back at the Samajwadi Party by putting up posters. The posters questioned: “Questions over donations to Ram Temple, silence over terror funding? Lord Ram is our faith, not a tool for politics.”

stories.title: Ghaziabad woman says ‘father’s intestines came out after stabbing’:'Husband used to beat me like monster'; son-in-law kills father-in-law
stories.summary: ‘I cannot explain what all my husband did to me. I kept tolerating it for years, hoping that he would change one day. But he used to drink alcohol and beat me like a cruel man. Six months ago, he broke both my ribs. This time, he came to kill me, but my father stepped in and lost his life while saving mine.’ Saying this, Monika, a resident of Modinagar in Ghaziabad, broke down in tears. Her brother standing nearby supported her and comforted her. Monika somehow composed herself. A medical representative (MR) husband killed his father-in-law in Ghaziabad on Thursday night around 10:30 pm. He stabbed his father-in-law five times in the stomach. When his wife rushed to save her father, the accused attacked her with the knife, injuring her hand. The injured wife Monika said, “Three days ago, my husband slapped me after drinking alcohol. I came to my parental home, but he came here to kill me. My father was suffering from blood cancer. He came in between to save me. That ruthless man did not spare my sick father either. He stabbed him in the stomach. My father’s intestines came out in front of my eyes.” Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Monika, who is devastated after her father’s murder. Read what the victim said… Sandeep said - 'I won't leave him alive today' Monika said, “On the night of July 9, around 10 pm, Sandeep came to my parental home in an intoxicated condition. He asked me to come with him. My father (Anar Singh) refused and said he would complain to the police. After this, Sandeep took out a knife and said, ‘I will not let you live today.’” “When Sandeep moved towards me, my father came in between. Sandeep then attacked my father repeatedly with the knife. When I tried to intervene, he slashed my hand with the knife. My thumb was cut and I received eight stitches. He also assaulted my mother and then fled.” Monica said - 'He had broken both my ribs' Monika said, “My husband had been physically abusing me after our marriage. When my son was born, he locked me inside a room and beat me. Six months ago, he broke both my ribs. Many times, I thought he would change, but his behaviour never improved.” “He assaulted me a month ago as well. After that, I came to my parental home. Two days before the incident, Sandeep was roaming around near our house and threatening me.” Monika said her father was suffering from blood cancer and was undergoing treatment. “We were praying to God for his recovery and long life, but I never imagined that my own husband would take my father’s life.” Now read the complete sequence of events... In Ghaziabad, medical representative Sandeep killed his father-in-law Anar Singh on Thursday night around 10:30 pm. He stabbed him five times in the stomach. When his wife came to intervene, he pushed her and escaped. According to police, Sandeep had slapped his wife three days earlier. Upset over this, Monika had gone to her parental home. On Thursday night, Sandeep reached his in-laws’ house to convince his wife to return with him. However, Monika refused to go with him. This angered him, and he started arguing with her. Hearing the commotion, his father-in-law Anar Singh scolded him and asked him to leave the house. Meanwhile, Sandeep took out a knife from his waist and repeatedly attacked his father-in-law. Hearing the screams, family members rushed in and took Anar Singh to hospital. He died during treatment at 8 am on Friday. Sandeep had a love marriage with Monika 19 years ago. The incident took place on Fafarana Road in Modinagar. Anar Singh (65), a resident of Modinagar’s Fafarana Road, was a retired employee of Modi Rubber Factory. He is survived by three daughters and one son. Sandeep Chaudhary, originally from Shikarpur in Bulandshahr, currently lives in the Brahmpuri area of Modinagar. Anar’s son Deepanshu told police, “My sister Monika, also known as Monu, had a love marriage with Sandeep. For the past one year, there had been disputes between my sister and brother-in-law. Sandeep used to harass her frequently. They had a dispute three days ago as well, due to which my sister came to our parental home. This angered my brother-in-law.” FIR of murder registered against brother-in-law In the murder case of Anar Singh, his only son Deepanshu Chaudhary lodged an FIR against his brother-in-law Sandeep Chaudhary at Modinagar police station. Police have detained the accused’s 18-year-old elder son. DCP Rural Surendranath Tiwari said: “Three police teams have been formed to arrest the main accused Sandeep Chaudhary. Police teams have also conducted raids in Bulandshahr in search of him.”

stories.summary: On Saturday at 5 AM, a speeding Eco car crashed into a stationary DCM in Rampur, UP. In the accident, four people sitting in the car died on the spot. Three were seriously injured. All were going from Delhi to Nainital for sightseeing. According to eyewitnesses, the DCM was parked on the roadside. The Eco car coming from behind must have been traveling at a speed of around 100kmph. The collision was so severe that the front part of the car was completely smashed. Its roof flew off. The people sitting in the car kept writhing inside. A video after the accident has surfaced. In it, a blood-soaked youth trapped among the corpses is pleading with people for help. He says, ‘Brother, save me’. After great effort, the police pulled out the bodies. The injured were taken to a nearby hospital. Police say that all 7 people in the car are said to be residents of Delhi-NCR. All were between 30 and 35 years of age. stories.title: Why Ayushman and ABHA cards matter:Free doctor fees, ICU care and surgeries, ₹5 lakh treatment cover; know how to apply from home
stories.summary: To provide financial assistance to poor and middle-class families during illness, the government is running the Ayushman Bharat Yojana. In a medical emergency, free cashless treatment up to ₹5 lakh is available. It is essential that every eligible member of the family has an Ayushman Card. The government is also creating ABHA cards for people. This is a digital health ID where your health-related information is securely stored. Blood test reports, X-rays, and prescription slips are also stored online here. Free treatment in this health scheme The Ayushman Bharat Yojana belongs to the central government. It was launched on 23 September 2018. Under this, needy families suffering from serious illnesses receive assistance of up to ₹5 lakh for treatment. Expenses include everything from hospital admission to medicines, doctor's fees, ICU costs, and even operation costs. The government covers expenses from 3 days before admission to 15 days after discharge. Under this scheme, more than 1,900 serious diseases like cancer, heart disease, kidney failure, liver disease, cataracts, knee replacement, and bypass surgery can be treated free of cost. The benefit is available only if admitted to the hospital for at least 24 hours. Expenses for cold-cough or doctor consultation in OPD (Outpatient Department) are not included. To cover families whose names were not included in this scheme, the UP government launched 'Mukhyamantri Jan Arogya Abhiyan' on March 1, 2019. The entire process, from getting the card made to receiving treatment in the hospital, has been kept the same for both schemes. How to find out where to get free treatment The benefits of this scheme can be availed in all government hospitals and listed private hospitals across the country. Follow these easy steps to find Ayushman hospitals in your district. If you do not have internet, you can also call the toll-free numbers 14555 or 1800-111-565 to ask for the name and address of your nearest Ayushman hospital. Ayushman Vay Vandana Card for elders above 70 years Your Ayushman card contains your photo, name, date of birth, QR code, and an ABHA number. When admitted to the hospital, you only need to show this card. You can use this card for treatment in any state or city across the country. The Ayushman card made for elders aged 70 years and above is called the "Ayushman Vay Vandana Card". Through this, senior citizens of all categories, including General/OBC and SC-ST, can avail free treatment up to 5 lakh. This applies regardless of their financial status or whether they possess any other private medical insurance. Getting an ABHA card is also very important Just as a bank account keeps a secure record of your financial transactions, similarly, the Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) digitally secures your medical history. This 14-digit unique health ID is linked to Aadhaar. If you go to a hospital for treatment, showing your ABHA card there allows the doctor to know your health condition. This is because it contains records of all your medical reports, doctor's prescriptions, tests, and medicines. This helps in starting the correct treatment quickly and avoids the need for repeated tests. Government hospitals offer scan share facility with ABHA card. Scanning the QR code generates a digital slip. This eliminates the need to stand in long queues at the registration counter. How to correct errors in Ayushman Card If there is an error in your Ayushman card's name, photo, or other information, log in to the Ayushman App and click on 'Redo e-KYC'. After this, perform OTP or face verification again using Aadhaar. If online correction is not possible, contact the Ayushman Help Desk or Nodal Officer at your nearest district hospital. If you haven't made an Ayushman card, you won't be able to get free treatment worth ₹5 lakh in a medical emergency. Also, without an ABHA card, you will have to carry old reports and prescriptions every time. The doctor will not get information about your old illness or medicines, which can increase the risk of delay or error in treatment.

stories.title: Thar submerged, highway boundary collapses in UP:Rivers overflow bridges as rain lashes 10 cities, alert issued for 75 districts
stories.summary: Monsoon rains are lashing Uttar Pradesh, with rivers in western UP overflowing. In several places, water is flowing over bridges. Heavy rainfall was recorded in 10 cities, including Lucknow, Sultanpur and Ayodhya, at around 12:30 am on Saturday. Intermittent drizzle continued until early Saturday morning. Clouds are covering most other cities, while some areas have also witnessed sunshine. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain and hailstorm alert for all 75 districts for the next 24 hours. An orange alert for heavy rainfall has been issued in 13 cities, while 27 cities are under a yellow alert. In Bijnor, the Ganga and its tributary Malan River are in spate. Traffic on several routes, including the Meerut-Bijnor Highway and Haridwar Road, has been stopped after water reached the bridges. In Hapur, a Thar SUV got submerged after an underpass filled with rainwater. It was pulled out with the help of a JCB. In Meerut, the boundary wall of a National Highway collapsed. A car got submerged due to waterlogging at a railway underpass, trapping two youths inside. Police rescued both of them by pulling them out with a rope. Fifteen people have died in the state in the last three days due to rain-related incidents. Ghaziabad has reported the highest number of deaths, with four fatalities. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed officials to visit affected areas and ensure immediate compensation for victims. Four boys swept away in Bijnor, canal breaches in Muzaffarnagar Earlier, due to heavy rainfall, four boys were swept away in strong river currents in two separate incidents in Bijnor at around 4 pm on Friday. One has been rescued, while the search for the others is underway. In Saharanpur, soil from a cemetery was washed away, exposing bodies buried in graves. In Muzaffarnagar, an overflowing canal breached. Meerut’s Mawana records highest rainfall in 24 hours In the last 24 hours, the highest rainfall in Uttar Pradesh was recorded in Mawana, Meerut, at 315 mm. It was followed by Jansath in Muzaffarnagar, which recorded 270.1 mm of rainfall. Weather scientist Atul Kumar Singh said: The rain system formed over the Bay of Bengal has now reached around Madhya Pradesh. Its impact is being felt in Uttar Pradesh, due to which the monsoon has intensified in the state. The rainfall spell is likely to continue for the next 3-4 days. Most cities are expected to receive light to moderate rainfall, while several areas may witness heavy to very heavy rain.

stories.title: Rajpal Yadav gets 3-month jail term in cheque bounce case:Delhi HC orders ₹7.35 crore payout, wife fined; says 'Law is not a film script'
stories.summary: The High Court awarded Rajpal a three-month jail term in each of the seven cheque bounce cases against him. All the sentences will run concurrently. Justice Swarnakanta Sharma directed officials to send the actor to jail. Justice Swarnakanta Sharma observed that Rajpal Yadav's conduct was questionable. The court said he had been given several opportunities to honour his commitment and repay the company's dues, but failed to do so. It added that he would now have to spend the next three months in prison. The court also remarked that the law is not a script that an actor can rewrite according to his own wishes. Court orders Rajpal to pay ₹7.35 crore The High Court granted Rajpal Yadav two months either to comply with the order or challenge the sentence before the Supreme Court. The court directed him to pay ₹1.05 crore to the complainant in each of the seven cases, taking the total compensation to ₹7.35 crore. It also clarified that nearly ₹2 crore already paid by the actor would be adjusted against the total amount. The case dates back to 2010, when Rajpal Yadav borrowed ₹5 crore to produce one of his films. After failing to repay the outstanding amount and the cheques issued by him bounced, the dispute turned into a prolonged legal battle. Rajpal had said, 'I am ready to go to jail five times, but will not pay a single rupee' Advocate Avneesh Sikka, appearing for Murli Projects Private Limited in the Delhi High Court, said all 21 petitions filed by Rajpal Yadav had been dismissed and the Sessions Court's verdict had been upheld. Rajpal's wife, Radha Rajpal Yadav, was also an accused in the case. The High Court ordered her to pay a fine of ₹5 lakh in each case. During the hearing, Rajpal's counsel sought probation for the actor, but the court rejected the request, observing that he had repeatedly failed to honour assurances given to the court. The court also noted that during the final hearing, Rajpal had said, "I am ready to go to jail five times, but I will not pay a single rupee." Loan taken for film Ata Pata Lapata Rajpal Yadav had decided to make his directorial debut with the film Ata Pata Lapata. To finance the project, he borrowed ₹5 crore from Murli Projects Private Limited. The film flopped at the box office, leaving Rajpal unable to repay the loan on time. The unpaid dues eventually led to the long-running legal dispute. Got six months sentence in 2018 In April 2018, a magistrate's court convicted Rajpal Yadav and his wife Radha in the cheque bounce case and sentenced the actor to six months in jail. In early 2019, the Sessions Court also upheld the conviction. Rajpal has been to jail in a cheque bounce case In June 2024, the Delhi High Court stayed Rajpal's sentence temporarily and directed him to clear nearly ₹9 crore in outstanding dues. However, he failed to deposit the amount within the stipulated time. On February 2 this year, the High Court ordered him to surrender. Rajpal surrendered before Tihar Jail authorities on February 5, 2026. After spending 12 days in jail, he was granted interim bail by the Delhi High Court on February 17. Shahjahanpur children sent piggy bank money, Rajpal also came to meet them Several film personalities had come forward to support Rajpal Yadav financially. Actor Sonu Sood was among the first to offer help, while former Bihar Chief Minister Lalu Prasad Yadav's son Tej Pratap Yadav announced financial assistance of ₹11 lakh. Children from Gurukul Seva Trust in Shahjahanpur also broke open their piggy banks and collected around ₹10,000 to help the actor. About a month ago, when Rajpal visited Shahjahanpur, he met those children to thank them personally.

stories.summary: The Ayodhya Ram Mandir offering theft case has taken a new turn. Suddenly, the atmosphere seems to be building in favour of Champat Rai, the former general secretary of the temple trust, while the entire blame seems to be falling on former trustee Anil Mishra. Question 1: What are the signs that Champat Rai is getting a clean chit? Answer: 5 major signs are emerging. Sign- 1: From the Trust to VHP, everyone has come out in support of Champat Sign- 2: The things that were accused of being stolen came to light Sign- 3: After the meeting, Champat Rai wrote a letter to the SIT Sign-4: Champat Rai's name is not in SIT's initial report Sign-5: Champat Rai presented his side after 1 month Question 2: Can Dr. Anil Mishra be made an accused? Answer: Yes, there are five indications for this as well. Indication- 1: The Trust considered Anil Mishra a suspect Indication- 2: Treasurer said - Hidden culprits should be caught Indication- 3: Serious allegations against Anil Mishra in SIT report Indication- 4: Allegation of taking 40% commission Hint- 5: No member of the trust is with Anil Mishra Question 3: What are the allegations against Anil Mishra as per SIT's preliminary report? Answer: According to SIT's preliminary report, Anil Mishra could be charged under sections 61 and 316 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Under the relevant sections, this could lead to a sentence of 10 years imprisonment. A separate FIR will not be registered to make him an accused. If the SIT recommends making Anil Mishra an accused in its final report, his name will be added to the existing FIR (registered on 25 June). stories.title: Youth shot dead after honking at bikers:Brother says local strongman opened fire after being asked to give way
stories.summary: A 25-year-old man was shot dead in Ghaziabad following a dispute over honking a motorcycle horn. His younger brother, who was with him at the time, was also injured in the firing. The biker allegedly honked to ask a vehicle to move aside, after which a local strongman opened fire with a pistol. One bullet hit the victim in the abdomen, while another struck the mobile phone kept in his pocket. The victim's family rushed him to Delhi's GTB Hospital, where he died during treatment. The incident took place at around midnight on Sunday in Ratiram Colony under the Loni Border police station area. Police identified the deceased as Vipin Kumar (25), a resident of Ratiram Colony. His younger brother Gaurav sustained a bullet injury to his hand. Police have arrested the main accused's father and wife. Police reached the spot soon after receiving information about the firing. The victim's family has demanded an encounter of the accused. Now the complete incident in detail Vipin's younger brother Gaurav said that their neighbour Pawan was hosting a party at his house in Ratiram Colony, where several relatives had gathered. After the party ended, Vipin and Gaurav accompanied some of the relatives to the nearby canal bridge so they could leave. While returning home, they got into an argument with a local man, Sonu, over honking the motorcycle horn. Gaurav told police that Sonu, along with his friends, opened fire on him and his brother. The first bullet hit Gaurav's hand. The attackers then fired two bullets at Vipin. One struck the mobile phone in his pocket, while the other hit his abdomen. Vipin worked at a factory in Shahdara, Delhi. Gaurav said - They killed brother in front of me Gaurav said they had gone to drop Pawan's relatives at the Loni Border canal bridge because it was late at night and the guests were unfamiliar with the route. On their way back, they found a group of youths standing on the road. When they honked to ask them to move aside, the youths allegedly said, "Don't you know who we are?" and immediately pulled out a pistol and started firing. "The first bullet hit me, but I survived. Two other youths were with us and they ran away. When I raised an alarm, the attackers fled. We rushed my injured brother to a nearby hospital. He was still breathing at that time. As his condition worsened, we shifted him to Delhi, where he died during treatment at around 2 am," Gaurav said. Pawan told police that the relatives attending the party at his house did not know the way, so they had escorted them to the Loni Border canal bridge on two motorcycles. While returning, an argument broke out with some youths standing on the road. He alleged that a youth named Sonu shot Vipin. According to Pawan, after Vipin collapsed to the ground from the first gunshot, the accused fired another shot. DCP Rural Surendranath Tiwari said an FIR has been registered on the complaint and the motive behind the murder is being investigated. Loni Border police have arrested the main accused Sonu's father, Brahmpal, a resident of Behta Hajipur under the Loni Border police station area. Sonu's wife Asha has also been arrested. 2 arrested including accused Sonu's wife Vipin's brother Azad Prajapati lodged a murder case at Loni Border police station. Police have arrested the main accused Sonu's father, Brahmpal, a resident of Behta Hajipur, and Sonu's wife Asha. The main accused, Sonu, is still absconding, and police are conducting raids to trace him.

stories.title: '₹15 lakh crore in my pocket,' says Gadkari:Rajnath-Yogi launch Lucknow-Kanpur expressway; journey cut to 40 minutes
stories.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari inaugurated the Lucknow–Kanpur Expressway in Unnao at 4 pm on Monday. They were accompanied by Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak. Following the inauguration, the leaders began their return journey to Lucknow by road via the newly inaugurated expressway. They had earlier travelled to Unnao by helicopter. Another official programme is scheduled later in the day in Sarojini Nagar, Lucknow. Expressway cuts travel time to 40 minutes The new expressway will reduce the travel time between Lucknow and Kanpur to just 40 minutes. At present, the journey typically takes between two-and-a-half and three hours. Constructed at Rs 4,700 crore, the expressway will be opened to the public from 8 am on Tuesday. The 63-km expressway is India's first barrier-free expressway, eliminating the need for vehicles to stop at toll plazas. However, motorists will pay significantly higher toll charges. A car travelling between Lucknow and Kanpur will pay Rs 275, compared with the previous toll of Rs 95. Two-wheelers barred, AI-based toll collection introduced Two-wheelers will not be allowed on the expressway. Vehicles will be permitted to travel at a maximum speed of 120 km/h. Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras and FASTag readers installed 500 metres before toll plazas will automatically deduct toll charges without requiring vehicles to stop. In the event of an accident, AI-enabled cameras will immediately send alerts to the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) control room. Built in 1,650 days The foundation stone for the Lucknow–Kanpur Expressway was laid on 5 January 2022. The project was inaugurated on 13 July 2026, meaning the expressway was completed in 1,650 days. stories.title: UP transfers 363 PCS officers, 8 moved out of Ayodhya:2 lists released in 12 hours, 91 women officers also shifted; check complete list
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has transferred 181 more Sub-Divisional Magistrates (SDMs). Before this, a transfer list of 182 Provincial Civil Service (PCS) officers was released late on Sunday night. Within just 12 hours, a total of 363 PCS officers have been transferred across the state. The list includes 91 women officers and 29 Yadav officers. In the list released on Sunday, 54 women officers and 18 Yadav officers were transferred, while Monday’s list included 37 women officers and 11 Yadav officers. Several SDMs who have been in the news recently are also part of the second transfer list. Among them is Garima Saunkia, who has been transferred from Auraiya to Sultanpur. Garima had secured the 30th rank in UPPSC-2021 and came into the spotlight after catching mass cheating during the UP Board examinations. During the action, she was allegedly misbehaved with and her mobile phone was also damaged. Barabanki SDM Rajesh Kumar Vishwakarma has also been transferred. Lawyers had earlier staged protests against him, accusing him of corruption. During the protest, demonstrators had smeared the government vehicle with paan stains. SDM Ankur Verma, who has been transferred from Saharanpur to Jaunpur, had also been in the news recently. A farmer had allegedly set himself on fire in Sarasawa, following which his family members levelled serious allegations against the SDM. After the incident, he was not given any new responsibility in the district. His name has now been included in the transfer list. Eight officers removed from Ayodhya Eight officers from Ayodhya have also been transferred in the second list. These include SDM Praveen Yadav, who has been sent to Ballia, SDM Shreya, who has been sent to Shravasti, and SDM Sudhir Kumar, who has been transferred to Sitapur. Assistant Municipal Commissioner of Ayodhya Municipal Corporation Ashok Kumar Gupta has been appointed as SDM in Sonbhadra. Meanwhile, Arvind Kumar III has been sent to Shamli, Ashok Kumar Saini to Mainpuri, Ram Prasad Tripathi to Mathura, and Abhishek Kumar Singh to Moradabad. See the complete transfer list... 182 PCS officers transferred here and there at midnight Earlier, 182 PCS officers were transferred at midnight on Sunday. The list included 54 women officers. According to the order, Kanpur Dehat SDM Surbhi Sharma was transferred to Baghpat, Ghazipur SDM Pushpendra Patel was sent to Ambedkar Nagar, and Unnao SDM Shubham Yadav was transferred to Bulandshahr. Varanasi SDM Pratibha Mishra was transferred to Kanpur Dehat, Mainpuri SDM Gopal Sharma was sent to Bareilly, and Rae Bareli SDM Mithilesh Kumar Tiwari was transferred to Mainpuri. Hathras SDM Lovegeet Kaur has been appointed as Officer on Special Duty (OSD) at Greater Noida Authority, while Amroha SDM Pushpanath Chaudhary has been transferred to Unnao. Devendra Pratap Singh, who was posted in UPEIDA, has been appointed as SDM in Jhansi. stories.title: 'Kathavachak' Abhinav Arora's Duster catches fire:Had come to Vrindavan with parents, sister; family escapes unhurt after spotting smoke
stories.summary: 'Kathavachak’ Abhinav Arora (10) Duster car suddenly caught fire in Mathura, around 2 AM on Sunday. He was returning to Delhi from Vrindavan with his parents and sister. As soon as the car reached the Yamuna Expressway, thick smoke started coming out. Immediately, Abhinav's father Tarun Arora, stopped the car. Everyone quickly got out and ran to stand at a distance. In no time, the car started burning fiercely. High flames began to rise. Meanwhile, the police and fire brigade were informed. The fire brigade team brought the fire under control after half an hour of effort. By then, the car had completely burned down. The incident is from the Sureer police station area. Abhinav was going from Delhi with his family According to the police, Delhi resident Kathavachak Abhinav Arora had come to Vrindavan with his family on July 11 in his Duster car. His father was driving the car. His mother was sitting in the front. His sister and Abhinav were in the back seat. Around 2 AM, as soon as they reached near milestone-84 on the Yamuna Expressway, they saw thick smoke coming out from the engine. The father immediately pulled the car to the side. Everyone quickly got out safely. The father called the police at Sureer police station area. Within a short time of receiving the information, the police and fire brigade team reached the spot. By then, the fire had completely engulfed the car. Crowd gathered on expressway, people started making videos Seeing the car burning, a crowd gathered on the expressway. People passing by stopped and started making videos. This caused a long traffic jam. The police explained to people and removed them from there. Traffic was streamlined. The police arranged for another vehicle. Abhinav Arora's family was sent to Delhi in it. In the initial investigation, the cause of the fire is being considered a technical fault. Family met with an accident within two days According to the police, Abhinav's family members said that within two days, their family had faced two accidents. The first accident happened on the night of July 11 while going from Delhi to Vrindavan. Even then, smoke had started rising from the engine. However, the situation was brought under control before the fire broke out. The second accident happened on the night of July 12 while returning from Vrindavan to Delhi. Who is Abhinav Arora ? Abhinav Arora is the son of writer Tarun Raj. He lives in Delhi. He is a 5th-class student in a private school. He is often seen in videos doing devotion to Lord Krishna and Ram. Abhinav has lakhs of followers on Instagram.

stories.title: Kaushambi mass marriage scam:Neighbour made groom to avail grant; father beats son at wedding ceremony
stories.summary: In Kaushambi, a young woman made a neighbouring youth sit in the wedding pavilion as a fake groom to receive the government grant under the Chief Minister's Mass Marriage Scheme. She had lured him by promising to give half of the grant money once it was received. The youth's father arrived at the spot. Seeing his son sitting in the pavilion dressed as a groom, he became furious and started beating him right there. When a commotion broke out, officials conducted biometric verification of both. While the young woman's fingerprints matched, the youth's fingerprints did not match the records. This exposed the fraud. On Sunday afternoon around 1 PM, 230 Hindu couples were married and 2 Muslim couples had their nikah performed under the Chief Minister's Mass Marriage Scheme at a guest house in the Sayara area of the city. The young woman had also registered for nikah in this scheme, but the young man with whom her nikah was fixed refused to participate in the mass marriage at the last moment. After this, the young woman made her neighbouring youth sit in the mandap. When the fraud came to light, the officials cancelled her registration. See the pictures The matter in detail On Sunday, a Chief Minister's Mass Marriage Programme was organised at a guest house located in Sayara area of the city. In this, 230 Hindu couples were to be married and two Muslim couples were to have their nikah. The nikah of a 19-year-old girl from Gulamipur village in Saini police station area was fixed with a youth from Raebareli. With the consent of both families, the date of nikah was also fixed for March 17, 2027. Despite this, the girl also got herself registered for nikah in the Chief Minister's Mass Marriage Scheme. Girl arrived, groom refused to come On Sunday afternoon around 1 o'clock, the young woman reached the event venue, but at the last moment, the young man from Raebareli refused to perform the nikah in the mass marriage ceremony. He said that he would come with the wedding procession on the scheduled date and perform the nikah from home itself, and would not participate in the mass marriage. When the groom did not arrive, the young woman and her mother called a young man living in the neighbourhood to obtain the government grant. It is alleged that he was lured with a share in the grant amount and made to sit as the groom in the wedding pavilion. The boy's father was on duty at the event The father of the young man, who was seated in the wedding pavilion, is a fourth-grade employee at Saini Fire Station. Coincidentally, he was on duty at the same mass marriage event. When he learned from fellow employees about his son sitting in the wedding pavilion, he reached the spot and in anger started beating him right there in the pavilion. This caused chaos at the venue. Amidst the commotion, officials conducted biometric verification of both. The young woman's fingerprints matched the records, but the young man's fingerprints did not match. After this, the entire fraud was exposed. Upon receiving information, police arrived and took the young woman, her mother, and the young man to the police station. Both parties clashed at the police station too At the police station, there was an argument and commotion between both parties. Police somehow calmed both parties down. After this, the young woman's registration was cancelled, while the young man was released with a warning. CDO Vinod Ram Tripathi stated, The young woman came to get married (nikah) with a different young man instead of her would-be husband. The young man's fingerprint did not match, so the nikah was not allowed to proceed. The marriage registration has also been cancelled. An investigation will be conducted into how both reached the wedding venue, and action will be taken.

stories.title: 'My Army man husband was beaten like a terrorist':Agra DSS's wife demands RPF personnel kneel and apologise, threatens suicide if they refuse
stories.summary: 'My husband has been in the Army, he was dragged like a terrorist. He had not committed any mistake. He was helping a woman during duty.' This is what Harendri Chahar, wife of Deputy Station Superintendent Narendra Chahar who was beaten up by RPF personnel in Agra, said. “The entire country has seen the video of my husband being beaten. We want justice along with his dignity. The RPF personnel who assaulted him should publicly apologize on their knees. If this doesn't happen, I will commit suicide,” Harendri said. On Sunday morning at 11 am at Agra Cantt Railway Station, a woman passenger could not board the train. Deputy Station Superintendent Narendra Chahar stopped the train to help her. After this, RPF personnel caught the woman on charges of chain pulling. A dispute arose over this matter. RPF personnel beat up Narendra Chahar. They dragged him to the police station. After the video of the incident surfaced, four RPF personnel were suspended. What Harendri Chahar said? Deputy Station Superintendent (DSS) Narendra Chahar's wife Harendri Chahar said, “My husband was dragged like a terrorist. Was he a thief, a rapist or a terrorist? He was helping someone else. Who does this during duty? The video has gone viral across the country. We want his lost honour back.” She said, “All four RPF personnel should kneel down at the same station and apologise to my husband. If the video of their apology doesn't come, I will commit suicide. The railway will be responsible for this.” 'Filed false case and beat him badly' Deputy Station Superintendent Narendra Chahar said, “A woman was running after a moving train. To save her life, I informed the guard via walkie-talkie to stop the train and safely helped the woman board the train. Shortly after this, RPF personnel arrived and falsely accused me of chain pulling.” “I explained to them that I had stopped the train, but they didn't listen at all. Instead they said - 'Is the railway your father's property?' After this, they snatched my mobile phone, abused me and started beating me. They also called auto-taxi drivers to beat me up. If this can happen to a station master on duty, then what must be happening to common people?” he asked. Father said even thieves are not treated like that Narendra's father Rajendra Singh Chahar said, “The RPF personnel have committed a crime against my son. Even a thief is not treated like this. Without any reason, he was threatened with death. The video of the incident is in front of everyone, yet no action has been taken even though several hours have passed. Until all four personnel who beat him are sent to jail, our protest will continue.” Nephew says tears came to his eyes Nephew Piyush said, “I was returning from the village. As soon as I saw the video, tears came to my eyes. Which son can watch his uncle being beaten like this, when he was performing his duty with complete honesty. We reached here crying with the family. An on-duty officer was mercilessly beaten by the personnel and auto drivers were also called to attack. This is the dictatorship of RPF.” Ex-serviceman says, ‘This is not just an insult to a soldier, but to the country.’ Manoj Chahar, who served 15 years in the Indian Navy with Narendra, said, “A former soldier was beaten like a terrorist. The four personnel who did the beating are sitting in the police station. Suspension alone will not do anything. After a few days they will be reinstated, but who will restore Narendra's dignity? The culprits should be dismissed and sent to jail. The incident happened at 11 AM, but even by night the DRM did not consider it necessary to talk.” Ex-servicemen organisations also came out in support Narendra Chahar is a resident of Akola Nagla Dayaram village in Agra. He joined the Indian Navy in July 2004. He retired after serving till 2019. In 2022, he was posted as Deputy SS in Railways. His family includes wife Harendri Chahar and two children. His daughter studies in Army School. His son is still young. After this incident, ex-servicemen organisations have come out in his support. They say that this is not just about a railway officer, but a matter connected to the honor of an ex-serviceman and the entire country. MP Rajkumar Chahar, who reached the Railway Institute on Sunday evening, took RPF officers to task saying, “You will defame the uniform and also defame our government. A video of the MP reprimanding RPF officers has surfaced on social media. In this, he is seen getting angry at RPF officers.” MP Rajkumar Chahar said, “I had to come here because of your actions. Who gave the order? One should have their own sense of how to deal with the public. Is this any way to drag and take away the Deputy Station Superintendent? You will defame the uniform as well as our government...such ill-mannered people.” Campaign on social media in support of railway officer. A campaign has also started in Narendra Chahar's support on social media. Instead of honoring Deputy SS Shri Narendra Singh Chahar who saved the life of a female passenger on AGC, he was humiliated by being dragged from the workplace by RPF personnel! There are also allegations of extorting ₹1000 from the woman. Video and statement are available. #JusticeForDySS #IndianRailways @RailMinIndia @RPF_INDIA AISMA BRC, a civil rights organisation, wrote on Twitter. The complete matter in detail On Sunday morning around 11 o'clock, the Amritsar to Hirakund Express train arrived at platform number-1. During this time, a female passenger got down from the same train and started buying some items. Just then the train started moving. The female passenger tried to board the moving train but could not get on. Upon this, Deputy Station Superintendent Narendra Chahar, stationed at the station, saw the woman running and informed the loco pilot via walkie-talkie and stopped the train. When the train's speed reduced, the woman started boarding it. Just then, an RPF personnel deployed there stopped the woman on charges of chain pulling. DSS Narendra Chahar opposed this. He said that he had stopped the train. However, the RPF personnel did not listen to him. A dispute arose between the two over this. Then it came to the point of a scuffle between them. RPF personnel slapped and dragged him away Meanwhile, the RPF personnel called his colleagues. After this, all of them caught DSS Narendra Chahar and started taking him away. When he protested, they grabbed him and threw him on the ground. This scuffle continued for about one minute. During this time, the staff present in Narendra Chahar's cabin kept telling the RPF personnel not to do this. However, ignoring them, the RPF team dragged the DSS to the RPF police station. During this time, the DSS kept struggling on the floor. However, four RPF personnel dragged him approximately 300 meters while holding his hands and feet. The RPF jawans allege that the DSS had misbehaved with them using abusive language. Railway employees protested, followed by suspension Railway employees gathered upon receiving information about the assault on the DSS. They started a protest demonstration outside the RPF station, raising slogans. They claim that the RPF treated them inhumanely for helping a female passenger. Following the incident, RPF ASI Meghraj Meena, ASI Balkishan, Constable Jitendra, and Badan Singh have been suspended. Subsequently, an inquiry committee has been formed. This committee includes the Senior Divisional Operations Manager, Senior Divisional Electrical Engineer, and Senior Divisional Security Commissioner (RPF). The committee will conduct an investigation and submit a report. After the report is received, strict departmental action will be taken against the guilty personnel. The railway administration has taken the matter seriously and assured an impartial investigation. Agra Railway Division's Public Relations Officer (PRO) Sanjay Gautam said, Four RPF personnel have been suspended for negligence in the DSS case. A three-member committee at JAG (Junior Administrative Grade) level has been constituted to investigate the incident.

stories.title: Western UP waits, eastern districts get rain:Gorakhpur streets flooded; Mayor steps into water with rolled-up trousers
stories.summary: Monsoon rain continues across Uttar Pradesh. In Gorakhpur, rainfall that began on Sunday evening continued until late at night, with heavy showers around 1 am. Roads and residential colonies were waterlogged. Mayor Dr Manglesh Srivastava rolled up his trousers and waded through the flooded streets to assess the situation, interacted with residents, and directed officials to improve drainage arrangements. Mayor inspects flooded areas after overnight rainfall Since Monday morning, skies have remained cloudy over 25 cities, including Ayodhya and Gorakhpur, while the rest of the state has witnessed clear weather and humid conditions. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for 22 cities in eastern Uttar Pradesh, with a heavy rainfall warning for eight of them. Note: Figures are valid up to 12 July 2026. Source: IMD Heavy rain alert issued for eight cities According to the IMD, the monsoon has weakened over western Uttar Pradesh as dry winds from Pakistan have pushed away monsoon clouds. As a result, rainfall is expected to remain subdued for the next three to four days, while humidity is likely to increase. Scattered showers are expected to continue in parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh. Rainfall remains seventeen per cent below the seasonal average The state was expected to receive an average of 11.1 mm of rainfall over the past 24 hours, but only 7.5 mm was recorded. Between 1 June and 12 July, Uttar Pradesh received 158.8 mm of rainfall, which is 17% below normal. Gorakhpur recorded the highest rainfall at 168 mm, followed by Bahraich with 129 mm, Ambedkar Nagar with 125 mm and Sant Kabir Nagar with 109.6 mm.

stories.title: Kashi, Mathura and Sambhal disputes:Hindu Muslim sides reject SC mediation proposal; both sides want verdict through trial
stories.summary: Stakeholders from The Hindu and Muslim sides on Monday rejected the Supreme Court's offer of mediation in three temple-mosque disputes in Uttar Pradesh. These three disputes relate to the Gyanvapi Mosque in Varanasi, the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi-Shahi Eidgah in Mathura, and the Shahi Jama Masjid in Sambhal. According to Bar Bench, the Supreme Court had sent a letter proposing mediation under the 'Samadhan Samaroh 2026' initiative for the peaceful resolution of these cases and sought consent from both parties. However, neither party gave their consent for this. Although information on when the court sent this letter has not come to light. Both parties have stated that they want a decision by fighting the case in court itself. In fact, a special Lok Adalat will be organized under the 'Samadhan Samaroh' from August 21 to 23 in the Supreme Court premises. Its objective is to find a solution through dialogue instead of a long legal battle. What you must know about all the disputes… 1. Gyanvapi mosque dispute (Varanasi) What is the dispute? The Gyanvapi Mosque, next to the Kashi Vishwanath Temple in Varanasi, is disputed. The Hindu side claims Mughal emperor Aurangzeb partially demolished the ancient Vishweshwar (Kashi Vishwanath) Temple in the 17th century to build the mosque. Demands of the Hindu community: 1. Declare the Gyanvapi complex as the ancient Vishweshwar Temple. 2. Allow regular Hindu worship inside the mosque complex. 3. Recognise the religious remains found there as part of the temple. Demands of the Muslim community: 1. Retain Gyanvapi as a mosque. 2. Reject new claims under the Places of Worship Act, 1991. 3. Protect Muslims' right to offer prayers at the mosque. Current status in the Supreme Court: Cases, including the ASI survey, are being heard in different courts. The Supreme Court has suggested resolving the dispute through a Lok Adalat (people's court). 2. Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi-Shahi Idgah dispute (Mathura) What is the dispute? The dispute concerns the Shahi Idgah Mosque near the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi in Mathura. The Hindu side claims the mosque was built after demolishing the temple at Lord Krishna's birthplace. Demands of the Hindu community: 1. Remove the Shahi Idgah Mosque. 2. Transfer the entire land to the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Trust. 3. Rebuild the temple. Demands of the Muslim community: 1. Recognise the mosque as a lawful place of worship. 2. Uphold the 1968 agreement and the Places of Worship Act, 1991. 3. Dismiss the petitions. Current status in the Supreme Court: Several cases are pending before the Allahabad High Court. The Supreme Court has also proposed resolving the dispute through a Lok Adalat. 3. Shahi Jama Masjid dispute (Sambhal) What is the dispute? The Hindu side claims the Shahi Jama Masjid in Sambhal was built after demolishing the ancient Harihar Temple. Demands of the Hindu community: 1. Conduct an archaeological survey of the mosque. 2. Restore the temple if remains are found. 3. Grant Hindus the right to worship. Demands of the Hindu community: 1. Recognise the mosque as a historic and lawful place of worship. 2. Stop the survey and fresh litigation. 3. Enforce the Places of Worship Act, 1991. Current status in the Supreme Court: Following the survey dispute and violence, the matter reached higher courts. The Supreme Court has also included it in its proposal for settlement through a Lok Adalat. Key questions regarding the issue 1. What did the Supreme Court propose? The Court asked both the Hindu and Muslim parties to try resolving the disputes through mediation. 2. Why did both sides reject the proposal? Both parties said they want the disputes to be decided by a final court verdict, not through a settlement. 3. What happens now? The Supreme Court will continue regular hearings, where both sides will present their evidence and arguments. 4. Is mediation completely ruled out? No. Although both sides have declined for now, the Court can reconsider mediation if they agree in the future. 5. Will this delay the cases? Yes. Since the disputes will go through the full judicial process, the final verdict may take time. 6. Will the Court examine the evidence? Yes. The Court will review documents, records, survey reports, and arguments from both sides. 7. Will this affect proceedings in lower courts? Yes. The future legal process will be guided by the Supreme Court's directions. 8. Can the Court force either side to settle? No. Mediation is voluntary and requires the consent of both parties. 9. What is the next key step? The disputes will now be decided through the Supreme Court's hearings and final judgment.

stories.title: Ram Mandir Trust invites applications for CEO post:SC seeks SIT report in donation theft case, next hearing on 20 July
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday issued notices to the Ram Mandir Trust and the Uttar Pradesh government in the Ayodhya Ram Mandir donation theft case. It also sought a status report from the SIT investigating the matter. The next hearing is scheduled for 20 July. A bench headed by Chief Justice Suryakant was hearing three separate petitions. The petitions sought to transfer the investigation to the CBI, constitution of a new SIT, and forming an expert committee to review various issues related to the management of temple donations. Meanwhile, Ayodhya Police will produce all eight arrested accused before the court through video conferencing. Their remand period ends today. During the hearing, police may seek seven-day remand of Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu, a close aide of former Ram Temple Trust general secretary Champat Rai, and Subhash Srivastava, who was in charge of counting donations. Earlier, police had taken accused Avinash, Anukalp, Lavkush and Karunesh on remand for questioning. The accused in the donation theft case have been kept in separate barracks at Faizabad Jail. Meanwhile, Jagadguru Paramhans Acharya of Tapasvi Chhawani said that if anyone has committed wrongdoing, they should not be spared. He claimed that Samajwadi Party leaders had no right to make allegations and alleged that they wanted to demolish the Ram Mandir and rebuild the Babri Mosque. According to sources, the team of Krishna Mohan, the interim general secretary of the Ram Temple Trust, may take charge after July 22. Discussions on the matter are underway.

stories.title: CM Yogi hears public grievances during Janata Darshan:Officials directed to resolve complaints on priority basis
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday listened to the problems of people from different districts of the state at Janta Darshan at his official residence, 5-Kalidas Marg. During this, he interacted with each complainant, took information about their grievances, and instructed the concerned officials to ensure timely and effective resolution of all matters on a priority basis. The Chief Minister said that resolving public problems is among the government's top priorities. He clearly told the officials that any kind of negligence or unnecessary delay in resolving complaints would not be tolerated. Instructions for serious action on every complaint During the Janta Darshan (public audience), the Chief Minister directed officials to conduct impartial investigations into every complaint and provide immediate relief to eligible individuals. He stated that complainants should not have to repeatedly visit government offices, and their problems should be resolved in a transparent and sensitive manner. The Chief Minister also said that officials should work with a spirit of public service, in line with the government's intention. Prompt resolution of common citizens' complaints is an important part of administrative accountability. Emphasis on making the public hearing system effective Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath told officials that complaints received during 'Janta Darshan' should be regularly reviewed, and in cases requiring immediate action, decisions should be taken without delay. He also instructed that the progress of grievance redressal should be continuously monitored, so that people can get timely justice and relief.

stories.title: ₹10,000 bounty smuggler arrested in Gorakhpur:Escaped police encounter 8 years ago, continued smuggling while on the run
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, a smuggler with a reward of ₹10,000, who was involved in illegal liquor trafficking, has been arrested by Khorabar Police. The smuggler had been absconding for 8 years. During his abscondence, he was involved in smuggling. Police cordoned off the Khorabar area and arrested him on Sunday morning around 10 AM. After interrogation, the accused was sent to jail in the evening after the court proceedings were completed. According to the police, after an encounter with the police in 2018, Virendra alias Hazari Singh, a resident of Sisar village, Hisar district, Haryana, had absconded. Two of his associates caught with a pickup truck full of liquor were sent to jail by the police. A few days later, a reward of ₹10,000 was also placed on him. Smuggler had escaped during the encounter SP City Nimish Patil said that on October 12, 2018, Khorabar police had seized a pickup truck full of liquor during an encounter on the four-lane bypass. It had two different number plates. Liquor smugglers used fake number plates to hide their identity. During the operation, Sonu alias Sawan and Praveen, residents of Sisar village in Hisar, Haryana, were arrested. During interrogation, the accused revealed that Virendra alias Hazari Singh, a resident of Sisar village, used to arrange for the supply of liquor and its dispatch to Bihar. After this, the police named him in the case, but he was absconding. The SSP had announced a reward of ₹10,000 for the arrest of the smuggler. On Sunday morning, Khorabar police, after cordoning off the area near Deoria Bypass, arrested Virendra alias Hazari Singh. In the evening, he was produced in court from where he was sent to jail.

stories.title: 3 Gorakhpur cops suspended for filming assault on woman:Stood by as attackers beat her; SHO, outpost in-charge also removed
stories.summary: Three police personnel have been suspended in connection with the assault on a young woman in the middle of a road in Gorakhpur. The SHO and the outpost in-charge have also been removed from their posts. A preliminary inquiry found that police personnel remained mere spectators while the woman was being assaulted. Instead of intervening to stop the attackers, some officers were seen recording the incident on their mobile phones. After the video surfaced, SSP Dr Kaustubh late Sunday night transferred Shahpur SHO Rakesh Roshan Singh and Kauwabagh outpost in-charge Durgesh Nandini to the police lines. Two constables of the Police Response Vehicle (PRV)—Raj Mangal Singh and Avinash Yadav—along with sub-inspector Abhishek Kumar Singh, who were seen in the video, were suspended. A report has also been sent recommending departmental action against Home Guard Haricharan Rai. Police have formed three teams to arrest the remaining accused. The main accused has already been arrested and sent to jail. He has been booked on charges including attempt to murder, molestation, assault and criminal intimidation. Police have also detained eight other suspects for questioning. July 9 Incident In the Shahpur police station area, on Thursday evening around 6:30 PM, youths in a black Scorpio grabbed the hair of a 24-year-old girl in the middle of the road and beat her, tried to tear her clothes, and touched her inappropriately. The girl kept pleading for help on the road. The girl alleges that the accused continued to assault and misbehave with her in the presence of the police, but the policemen remained silent spectators. The case is from the Shahpur police station area. Based on the girl's complaint, an FIR was registered on Friday morning around 10 AM against unknown bike riders and youths in a black Scorpio. One accused has been arrested. The video of the incident surfaced on Saturday. The young woman was going to the Railway Hospital by car to get her father treated. On the way, her car collided with a bike. After this, an argument ensued between both parties. It is alleged that the bike rider called his friends. Within a short time, youths who arrived in a black Scorpio attacked the young woman and started assaulting her. The full story A 24-year-old woman, a resident of Ramgarhtal police station area, told the police that she was going to the Railway Hospital in a Grand Vitara car to get her sick father treated. On the way, a bike rider collided with her car. The woman alleged that as soon as the bike rider got out of the car, he started misbehaving with her and repeatedly pressured her to apologize. The woman refused to apologise, stating that the fault was the bike rider's. On this, the dispute between the two escalated. After some time, the bike rider called his companions. It is alleged that the youths who arrived in a black Scorpio grabbed the woman's hair and started assaulting her. They abused her, tried to tear her clothes, and touched her inappropriately. After this, they vandalized the car and broke its window. As they left, the accused fled after threatening her with rape and death. Misbehavior with the young woman in front of the police According to the young woman, the accused continued to assault and misbehave with her for a long time. She kept screaming for help, but the accused remained fearless. Policemen were present at the spot, yet the accused did not stop. After the incident, the young woman informed the police and her family. She stated that she could identify the accused if they came forward. Assault seen in the video In the viral video of the assault, some youths are seen grabbing a girl by her hair and beating her. The accused also break her car's window and appear to hit her head with a heavy object. Five policemen are also visible at the scene in the video. During this, the accused continue to assault and misbehave with the girl. Many local people were also present at the scene. Meanwhile, the girl's ailing father is seen standing at some distance with support. One accused arrested, others being identified says SP City SP City Nimish Patil said- An FIR has been registered on the complaint of the young woman. One accused has been arrested. He is a resident of Mohanapur, Padri Bazar. Some suspicious youths are also being interrogated.

stories.title: Sleeper Vande Bharat Express to run between Varanasi and Chheharta:PM Modi to flag off train on July 17, service to operate thrice a week
stories.summary: The country's second sleeper Vande Bharat Express train will run between Varanasi and Chheharta in Amritsar. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will flag it off from Jalandhar on July 17. This train will be named Sant Ravidas Express. The train's schedule has been released by the Railways. The Prime Minister will flag it off from Jalandhar via video conferencing. On the same day, the PM will inaugurate Jalandhar's new railway station. Operation will be three days a week According to the letter issued by the Railway Board, the Vande Bharat sleeper train running from Chheharta to Varanasi will be named Sant Ravidas Express. Its train number has been kept as 14624/14623. It will operate only three days a week. Train number 14624 from Chheharta will run every Wednesday, Friday, and Sunday at 2:05 PM. Train number 14623 from Varanasi will run every Thursday, Saturday, and Monday at 7:05 PM. And will reach Chheharta at 5:10 PM the next day. Train Schedule Stoppages at these stations The Vande Bharat Sleeper Express train will have stoppages between Varanasi and Chheharta at Jaunpur City, Sultanpur, Lucknow, Shahjahanpur, Bareilly, Moradabad, Saharanpur, Ambala Cantt, Ludhiana, Jalandhar City, and Amritsar. The primary maintenance of the train will be at Chheharta station.

stories.title: Cheating gang targeting Boring Technician exam arrested:UP STF nabs candidate from Varanasi and solver from Prayagraj; FIR filed against 13
stories.summary: A case of cheating using electronic devices has come to light during the Assistant Boring Technician examination of the Minor Irrigation Department in Varanasi. Two candidates were caught cheating in the examination conducted by the Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission. In the same case, the UP STF has arrested the gang leader helping candidates cheat and 11 other people from Prayagraj. The candidates paid ₹5 lakh each to Captain Singh Patel, the mastermind of the cheating gang. Currently, cases have been registered against the 13 accused caught from Varanasi and Prayagraj at Kotwali and Sigra police stations. The examination was under STF surveillance when officials received inputs about cheating. STF Inspector Anil Kumar Singh informed that the field unit Varanasi was active during the examination. During this time, officials received information that a gang involved in cheating in competitive examinations using micro-electronic devices after collecting large sums of money. Following this, the team coordinated with the Prayagraj unit and started the investigation. During this, officials learned that Shivjeet Patel, the ringleader of the gang facilitating cheating through micro-electronic devices, and his brother Captain Singh Patel were present with solvers in a room in Kothari village, Bahariya police station, Prayagraj. Solvers were answering questions for two candidates through electronic devices. Acting on this information, the STF Varanasi team raided the location and arrested the gang leader and solvers from there. Two candidates arrested from Harishchandra Balika and Anglo Muslim School Anil Kumar Singh stated that an STF team, based on the tip-off, arrested one candidate from each examination centre carrying an electronic device from Harishchandra Balika Inter College located in Maidagin and Anglo Muslim School in Lallapura area. Gang charged ₹5 lakh from each candidate The accused revealed during interrogation that Captain Singh Patel, his brother Shivjeet Patel, Deepak Patel, and Rajendra Yadav alias Dhirendra Yadav have an organized gang for cheating in competitive exams. The racket was masterminded by Shivjeet Patel. They all contact certain candidates appearing in various competitive exams through their relatives and acquaintances, gaining their trust that they will clear the examination with the help of a solver. In return, ₹5 lakh was charged. Those arrested include:

stories.title: Free treatment up to ₹5 lakh, ₹1.60 crore accident cover:UP teachers and non-teaching staff can apply; these documents are mandatory
stories.summary: Government teachers in UP will get accidental insurance of ₹1 crore 60 lakh and cashless treatment up to ₹5 lakh. The insurance will provide financial security in case of a major accident. Cashless treatment will cover hospital expenses during serious illness. Shikshamitras, instructors, and cooks will also be covered under this scheme. Approximately 12 lakh teachers and non-teaching staff of the Basic and Secondary Education Department will benefit from this. This facility will be provided under the "Chief Minister Teacher Cashless Medical Scheme". All Education Department Staff to Get Accidental Insurance This facility will be available under SBI's Corporate Salary Package (CSP). If a teacher dies in a road, rail, or air accident, their nominee will receive an insurance amount of up to ₹1.60 crore. If a teacher becomes completely disabled in an accident, they will receive insurance benefits according to the prescribed rules. Normal death due to illness or heart attack is not covered under this insurance. Cashless treatment up to ₹5 lakh will also be free This facility will be available under the Chief Minister Teacher Cashless Medical Scheme, which will be operated by SACHIS. It is a government agency, whose full name is State Agency for Comprehensive Health and Integrated Services. If a teacher or their dependent family member falls ill and is admitted to a hospital, cashless treatment up to ₹5 lakh per year can be availed in UP's government hospitals, medical colleges, and private hospitals associated with SACHIS. This facility will be available again every year. Create a Cashless Medical Card in 10 Simple Steps Register by September 6 Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had announced the Chief Minister Teacher Cashless Medical Scheme last year on Teacher's Day (September 5). The Chief Minister formally launched the scheme on July 8, 2026. All eligible teachers and non-teaching staff must complete their and their family's registration by September 6, 2026, so that the verification process can be completed. According to Archana Verma, CEO of SACHIS, a portal has been created for the registration, verification, and issuance of health cards for teachers. More than 7.89 lakh beneficiaries from the Basic Education Department have already registered their data. The portal for the Secondary Education Department has also been launched. Soon, teachers from the Higher Education Department will also join this scheme. After verification and e-KYC, teachers will be able to download their health cards and avail the benefits of cashless treatment. Not a single rupee to be paid from pocket According to the government order, the annual premium for a teacher under this scheme will be around ?3,000. The entire payment will be made by the government from its departmental budget. Employees will not have to pay a single rupee of premium from their own pockets. This scheme will be applicable only after the patient is admitted to the hospital. It will benefit in the treatment of more than 1900 diseases including cancer, heart disease, kidney disease, neuro, and surgery. OPD expenses for common cold or just consulting a doctor and taking medicine are not included in this. Answers to 4 important questions for teachers and staff Question 1- What do I need to do to avail the benefits of cashless treatment and insurance scheme? Answer- To avail cashless treatment, you will need to register on the portal of the Education Department and 'SACHIS'. After this, the department will issue you a 'Cashless Health Card'. Your salary account must be with SBI. Question 2- If an unfortunate incident happens to an employee within the hospital, how will the money for children's education and marriage be received? Answer- If an accident happens to an employee, the family will not only receive insurance money. Separate financial assistance will also be provided for children's education and daughters' marriages. Necessary documents will have to be submitted for this. After the investigation is complete, this amount will be sent directly to the bank account. Question 3- Will this facility also be valid in hospitals outside UP? Answer- This facility will only be available in UP government hospitals and private hospitals associated with 'Sachis'. No money will be taken from the patient. More than 1900 treatment packages are already fixed. Therefore, the government will directly pay the hospital. Question 4- What are the conditions for the ?2 lakh cover being provided to cooks and contract workers? Answer- Cooks and other contract employees earning less than ?10 thousand will have a zero-balance account opened in SBI. Upon activation of the debit card, an accidental insurance of ?2 lakh will be provided. No separate paperwork will be required for this.

stories.title: Married lovers die by suicide in Kanpur hotel:Man records reel before death; woman tells husband she consumed poison
stories.summary: In a hotel in Kanpur, a couple died by suicide by consuming poison. The woman was from Unnao and the man was from Fatehpur. Both were married and had left their respective homes with a plan to die. The incident came to light on Saturday evening at 4 PM, when a screaming sound came from the hotel room. When the hotel staff opened the door with another key, the young man was lying unconscious on the bed, while the woman was lying nearby and screaming for water. Both were taken to Ursala Hospital, where doctors declared both of them dead. On Sunday, police investigation revealed that before reaching the hotel, the young man had made a reel on Instagram. In which he had said, “If I write a book of my pain, people will be afraid of love...”. He also wrote, "I am going to die". Meanwhile, the woman called her husband and said, “I have consumed poison, now live happily with the children...” and then cut the call. About a month ago, both of them left their families and fled to Gujarat, from where the police recovered them and handed them over to their relatives. Despite the strictness of the family and the police, both came into contact again and decided to die together when the path to living together was closed. Based on call details, social media posts, and chats, the police are investigating the entire matter, considering it a pre-planned suicide. The post-mortem of both bodies was conducted on Sunday evening around 4 PM. Shivangi ran away with her lover on June 9 On Saturday, police found two bodies at Hotel Surya located at Ghantaghar in Kanpur. They were identified as Shivangi (33) from Unnao and Digvijay (35), a young man from Fatehpur. Dheeru Tiwari, a resident of Magarwara, Unnao, works in the travel business in Gujarat. At home, he has his wife Shivangi, a seven-year-old daughter, and a nine-year-old son. Dheeru stated that his life was going very well, but a year ago, his wife Shivangi became friends with Digvijay, a resident of Radha Nagar, Fatehpur, through Facebook. Dheeru said, "I lived in Gujarat. Shivangi and Digvijay took advantage of this, and their closeness grew. When the family became aware of the matter, I also protested. When the discord increased over this issue, on June 9, 2026, Shivangi left me and the children and ran away from home with her lover Digvijay." According to the police, Shivangi's husband Dheeru Tiwari and brother Himanshu Shukla registered a missing person report for Shivangi at the police station. The police recovered both of them from Gujarat. Both were released on the condition that they would no longer have any relationship with each other. Even both their SIM cards were broken at the police station. After this, both started using new mobile numbers, but within a month, they started talking again. Both decided to die together due to restrictions. After spending three hours together in the hotel room, they committed suicide on Saturday afternoon. Shivangi called her husband and said - now live happily ACP Collectorganj Anand Kumar Ojha said, “Digvijay, a resident of Radha Nagar, Fatehpur, and Shivangi, a resident of Magarwara, Unnao, checked into the hotel on Saturday afternoon at 12:30 PM. Both were staying in room number 106.” At 4 PM, Shivangi's scream was heard from the room. She was screaming, asking someone to give her water. A packet of poison was also recovered from the room. Her husband, Dhiru, said that Shivangi called him after consuming poison and said, "I have consumed poison. Now live happily with the children..." After this, the call was disconnected. After the call was disconnected, Dhiru informed the Unnao police about the matter. Unnao police contacted Kanpur's Collectorganj police based on the location and received information about both of them committing suicide. At the post-mortem house on Sunday evening, relatives of both were repeatedly saying that it had been about 13 years since Shivangi's marriage and she had two children. Digvijay also had a wife and children, but both were so misguided that they first abandoned their spouses and children and ran away. When the police and family members became strict, both decided to die together. If I write a book of my pain, people will be scared of love ACP Kalaktarganj stated that Digvijay, before his death, uploaded a reel with a song from Fatehpur station on his Instagram account. It features the song 'If I write a book of my pain, people will be scared of love'. Along with this, he had written that 'I am going to die'. Just a few hours after uploading this video, Digvijay and Shivangi committed suicide. Not only this, before committing suicide, Digvijay had also posted several crying and painful videos on Instagram. Shivangi was practicing law Digvijay was a coach attendant in the Railways. Shivangi's brother said that after completing her law studies, she was practicing in Unnao Court. But during this time, she somehow came into contact with Digvijay, and their closeness increased to such an extent that, disregarding social shame and decorum, both first ran away from home.
