stories.summary: In Kanpur, on Monday morning at 6 AM, a Scorpio crashed into a parked truck on the National Highway. In the accident, three people, including two children, died on the spot. Five people were seriously injured. The collision was so severe that the car was torn to pieces. Half of the car was completely destroyed. People got trapped inside. People writhed in pain. They kept pleading for help. Passersby informed the police. Police, who arrived at the scene, started the rescue operation. With the help of a gas cutter, the car was cut open to pull people out. The injured were taken to Kanshiram Hospital. The bodies were sent for post-mortem. According to the police, about eight people were traveling in the Scorpio. The car's speed was over 100 kmph. stories.title: Ram Mandir theft accused's family hides in old mud home:Main house locked; brother says, 'Leave us alone, we're tired of answering'
stories.summary: A low-ranking employee in Uttar Pradesh's Pratapgarh, Avinash Shukla's story reads like a movie script. He appeared to transform his fortunes overnight, acquiring two houses within months leaving villagers stunned. His sudden rise came under scrutiny on June 4, when police recovered ₹20.39 lakh in cash and 1,121 US dollars from his house, raising questions about the source of his wealth. A Dainik Bhaskar team visited Avinash's home in Pratapgarh and found it locked. About 50 metres away, his family was found hiding in a mud house. On seeing the reporters, Avinash's brother became agitated and said, "Please leave us alone. We're exhausted from answering people's questions." His father added that the matter is before the Ayodhya court and any answers would come through the legal process. The visit made two things clear: first, the family no longer wants to face villagers; second, they have grown weary of constant questions following the police raid and Avinash's arrest. Read our special ground report... Locals say Avinash's family has disputes with many Nariawan village is about 40 km from Pratapgarh district headquarters. A narrow road through the fields leads to Avinash's house in Babupur. When our team tried to talk to the villagers on camera, they said, “Why do you make us fight? Many people in the village already have disputes with Avinash's family.” People said Avinash's father Ram Sajeevan is a farmer. His family owns about 13 bighas of land. Avinash is the youngest of five brothers. Three elder brothers -- Lalit, Amit, and Anuj -- do farming work at home. Dhaba, shop all closed, family running on farming Money for running Avinash's household came only from farming. Elder brothers Lalit and Amit together opened a dhaba on the road from Fatehpur to Kanpur. But, it had to be closed down in a short time. Lalit then opened a paan shop outside the village. This also did not run well. So, it also had to be closed. Due to the family's financial hardship, Abhishek, Avinash's elder brother, went to Ayodhya about 10 years ago. He was living in Shyam Sadhanalaya Yoga Center in Kaushalpuri. There he served Dr. Chaitanya Guru. Then he became a teacher in his yoga center. Avinash left studies, started selling shoes Avinash's mind was not in his studies. He had dropped out after 10th grade. Derwa market is about 15 kilometers away from home. Avinash started working at a shoe store there. He used to get ₹5,000. However, after working for some time, he left it all. He started insisting to his family to get him an e-rickshaw, which he would drive in the city. But the family did not have enough money to get Avinash an e-rickshaw. Elder brother called him to Ayodhya, got him a job in the temple Avinash told his elder brother Abhishek about his problem. A year and a half ago, he called Avinash to a yoga center in Ayodhya. He recommended Avinash to some people and got him a job at the Ram Temple. This was the opportunity that changed the family's fortune. Manoj Shukla, former Block Head of Babaganj, says, “We don't know this family directly. It's true that until two years ago, this family had nothing. They had opened a paan shop here, which didn't work out. When the theft was exposed, we found out. It seems like a small-scale theft, like a pinch of salt in the dal. But, the big fish hasn't been caught yet.” Family misleading by locking the permanent house from inside Understanding the village atmosphere, our Dainik Bhaskar team reached the place where Avinash's house is located. This white-colored house had a channel gate for entry. It was locked from the inside. No one came out when called. About 50 meters away is a mud house. This is where Avinash's father and his entire family used to live. We reached there. Here we met Avinash's father, brother Amit, and their mother. They flared up as soon as they saw us. They said, “We don't want to talk. The matter is in Ayodhya Court, go there.” Amit said, “I know that some people from the village itself are calling the media from outside and defaming us. Leave from here immediately... otherwise it won't be good.” We explained that they should present their side. Another house built in two years, all facilities available here A new house is being built about 50 meters away from this old house. Villagers said that Avinash is building this house. Some laborers were present in this house, who were making the floor. The house has gates on 3 sides. The entire house has tiles. Indian and Western toilets are also built. This means that all the necessary things should be present here. Villagers say this house was completely ready in just two years. Stealing where we bow our heads is wrong Ram Bahadur from the same village says, “Offerings should not have been stolen from Ram Temple. In the temple where we go, where we bow our heads, if theft is happening there, it's not a good thing.” We asked if the accused of theft is from his own village, Ram Bahadur replied, “We don't have information about this.” Elder son's wedding was normal, second son's had a grand function We asked the villagers - a picture of Avinash's elder brother Amit had surfaced. In it, he was seen standing with lakhs of rupees in his hand. People said this picture was from the time of his wedding. Amit got married on February 25. It is said that Avinash spent about ₹6 lakh on this function. The wedding took place at Ram Janaki Guest House in Lalganj Ajhara. Many videos related to weddings and Haldi have surfaced. A villager attending the wedding says - the first son's wedding didn't have a good function. But, the second son's wedding was very grand. Bought a second-hand Brezza, told friends - enjoy yourselves Avinash bought an old Brezza car last year. The car cost ₹3.5 lakh. He used to travel to and from the village in this car. He would throw parties for his friends in the village. He spent a lot of money. If friends asked him to get them a job like his, he would say, “You guys eat and drink, tell me where you need something... don't try to know more than that.” ₹2.5 lakh transferred to Avinash's girlfriend's account After the arrest, discussions quickly arose that Avinash's marriage had broken off. After reaching the village, it came to light that Avinash also has a girlfriend in Ayodhya. Avinash had gifted her an iPhone. He had transferred ₹2.5 lakh to her bank account. He often used to gift her jewelry. Police also found 11 grams of gold and 375 grams of silver jewelry from Avinash's house. When the police interrogated Avinash, he admitted all this. The police have not yet questioned that girl. Villagers say that there is no information about his relationship with any girl in Pratapgarh. Ayodhya Yoga Center expelled Avinash's brother As soon as Avinash's name came up in the Ram Mandir offering theft case, Shyam Sadhanalaya Yoga Center expelled Avinash's brother Abhishek from there. Police investigated this yoga center in Kaushalpuri multiple times. From here, on June 28, a box labeled 'Ramrajya Kosh' was also found. It had a Paytm QR code on it. Several documents related to Ram Mandir were also found. So far, the investigation has revealed that theft of ₹60 lakh to ₹70 lakh was committed solely by Avinash. stories.title: UP transfers 182 PCS officers overnight:54 women among them; Deepika Meher posted as Shamli SDM, Lavgeet Kaur sent to Noida
stories.summary: In Uttar Pradesh, 182 Provincial Civil Service (PCS) officers were transferred late on Sunday night. Among them are 54 women officers. Under the order issued by the government, Sub-Divisional Magistrates (SDMs) of several tehsils have been changed, while some officers have been given new responsibilities. According to the order, Surabhi Sharma, SDM of Kanpur Dehat, has been sent to Baghpat, Pushpendra Patel, SDM of Ghazipur, to Ambedkar Nagar, and Shubham Yadav, SDM of Unnao, to Bulandshahr. Pratibha Mishra, SDM of Varanasi, has been posted to Kanpur Dehat, Gopal Sharma, SDM of Mainpuri, to Bareilly, and Mithlesh Kumar Tiwari, SDM of Raebareli, to Mainpuri. Lavgeet Kaur, SDM of Hathras, has been made Officer on Special Duty (OSD) in Greater Noida Authority, while Pushpnath Chaudhary, SDM of Amroha, has been sent to Unnao. Devendra Pratap Singh, posted in Uttar Pradesh Expressways Industrial Development Authority (UPEIDA), has been made SDM of Jhansi. Additionally, Pragya Pandey, SDM of Hasanganj tehsil of Unnao, has been sent to Barabanki, Ajendra Singh from Kaushambi to Unnao, and Abhinav Yadav from Misrikh tehsil of Sitapur to Jalaun. Meanwhile, Akanksha Gautam has been made Sub-Divisional Magistrate of Sonbhadra from Sitapur, and Shikha Shukla of Kanpur Nagar from Sitapur. stories.title: 72 wrestlers to get training at Sigra SAI NCOE:Wrestlers from UP, Haryana, Punjab, Maharashtra and Karnataka arrive; Dronacharya awardee leads selection
stories.summary: Selection trials for wrestling training are underway at the NCOE Centre, started by SAI in Varanasi. More than 150 wrestlers are showcasing their skills in this. For this center, 36 male and 36 female wrestlers will be selected in different categories. A representative from TIDEC Delhi has been nominated to conduct these selection trials, under whose supervision they are currently underway. Two Dronacharya awardees, Mahasingh Rawat and Mahavir Prasad, and Chief Coach Sahil Sharma from Lucknow SAI are present. See three pictures Selection will be for 36-36 seats Regarding the selection, Deputy Director Sigra SAI NCOE Shubhanshu Dwivedi informed - Currently, trials for the wrestling discipline are being held by SAI for this NCEO centre. This selection is for the residential scheme. We have 36-36 seats in the men's and women's categories. The entire vacancy will be filled. In the junior category, we will also keep two to three seats vacant in case any wrestler is unable to join, as these are admission seasons. In the senior category, there will only be one or two on the waitlist. The final list will be released this evening Shubhanshu Dwivedi informed - We will finalise a list of 60 to 70. Out of which, 36-36 wrestlers will be taken for the final selection trial. To ensure the integrity of this entire process, Sahil Sharma, who has been a Dronacharya awardee and coach to Sakshi and Vinesh Phogat, is conducting the trials. The final list will be released by the evening of July 17.

stories.title: CM likely to visit in Gorakhpur on July 22:6-lane flyover inauguration may take place, BJP booth conference on agenda
stories.summary: CM Yogi will reach Gorakhpur on July 22. On the same day, he will inaugurate the city's first six-lane flyover. On July 22 itself, BJP is going to organize booth conferences simultaneously in all assembly constituencies of the state. The booth conference for Gorakhpur Urban and Gorakhpur Rural assembly constituencies will be held at Yogiraj Baba Gambhirnath Auditorium. The Chief Minister will also participate here. During this visit, the Chief Minister may also attend the Shri Ram Katha starting from July 23 at Gorakhnath Temple. The Chief Minister's program has not been officially confirmed yet, but the administration has started preparations. The Chief Minister may arrive in Gorakhpur on the morning of the 22nd. First, he will participate in the BJP's booth conference organized at Yogiraj Baba Gambhirnath Auditorium. 829 booth presidents from Gorakhpur Urban and Gorakhpur Rural assembly constituencies will participate in this conference. MP Ravi Kishan, Gorakhpur Rural MLA Vipin Singh, Mayor Dr. Manglesh Srivastava, and Metropolitan President Ramesh Gupta will also participate in this. The Metropolitan Committee has started preparing for this event. Flyover built at a cost of 429 crores The Chief Minister will inaugurate the six-lane cum four-lane flyover, which has been constructed at a cost of 429 crore rupees. The six-lane flyover starts from the petrol pump near Indira Nagar on the Padleganj-Nausad road and ends approximately 2.2 kilometers ahead of the Transportnagar police outpost. A roundabout is also being built on the Deoria bypass. From here, a four-lane bridge is being lowered onto the Deoria bypass. Its length is approximately 400 meters. If both bridges are combined, the total length is more than 2600 meters. With the construction of this bridge, travel on the Lucknow route will become even easier. The problem of traffic jams at Deoria Bypass, Nahar Road Tiraaha, Rustampur Chauraha, Falamandi Chauraha, and Transportnagar Chauraha will be resolved. People will be able to start from Padleganj and go directly to Transportnagar. Those who need to go towards Deoria Bypass can descend onto that road directly from above.

stories.title: Marriage refusal ends in gun attack:Woman shot on road; suspect shouts, 'I won't let you be anyone else's'
stories.summary: A 24-year-old woman was shot by her alleged stalker in the middle of a road in Uttar Pradesh's Meerut after she refused his marriage proposal. The accused stopped the woman and her friend late on Thursday night, asked her to marry him, and opened fire when she said no. The woman was seriously injured and is undergoing treatment at a hospital. As the accused fled, he allegedly shouted that if she would not marry him, he would not let her marry anyone else. Police have registered a case and launched a search for the accused. The incident is being investigated further. 2 pictures from after the incident Now, understand the entire matter in a sequential manner Despite being married, he was pressuring her for marriage Ayesha said - The accused Ballu lives near the Gaddha Wali Masjid. He is married. He married his maternal uncle's daughter. Despite this, he was pressuring Shaheen for marriage. He had been harassing her for a long time. My friend often told me about this. She used to ask for ways to get rid of him. She didn't go to the police for fear of defamation. We didn't know it would come to this. Brother said - Sister came home 5 days ago The brother said - We are three siblings. The eldest sister, who was shot, works at a beauty parlor in Shyamnagar. She had come home 5 days ago. The police arrived at 1 AM, and that's when we learned about the incident. Girl undergoing treatment, investigation ongoing After receiving information about the incident, the police from Brahmapuri and Lisari Gate police stations, along with the SP City, reached the spot. SP City Vinayak Gopal Bhosle said that information about firing was received. So far, the investigation and questioning suggest a case of unrequited love. The girl is undergoing treatment. The police are investigating based on all facts and evidence.

stories.title: 'Oh Allah, I won't slaughter cows anymore':Bareilly cattle smuggling suspect screams after police firing; 40 kg meat found at home
stories.summary: In Bareilly, a cow smuggler was arrested in an encounter around 10 PM on Thursday night. The accused was shot in the leg during the encounter, after which he was arrested. After being injured, the accused cried out, "Oh Allah... I made a mistake, I will never slaughter cows again." Earlier on Thursday afternoon, police raided the accused's house and recovered about 40 kg of beef, four legs of cattle, and animal slaughtering tools. During the operation, 3 people, including the main accused, had fled. During the late-night search, the accused fired at the police team, after which he was injured in retaliatory action. This encounter took place in the Izzatnagar police station area. Now read the full case in detail Cow's leg found in house during raid According to the police, on Thursday around 12 noon, information was received that cow slaughter was being carried out at the house of Akiluddin alias Gattu in Mahlau village. As soon as the information was received, Izzatnagar police station reached the spot and raided. Seeing the police, the accused present there started fleeing. During the operation, the police arrested Mohammad Khan from the spot, while the main accused Akiluddin, his accomplice Alam, and Haseena fled. During the search, the police found about 40 kg of beef, four legs of cattle, and tools used for slaughtering animals. Police interrogation revealed that Akiluddin is the main accused of this entire gang. He used to slaughter cows. After this, the police registered a case against him and other accused and started searching for them. Seeing himself surrounded, the accused fired at the police Late at night, the police were raiding in search of Akiluddin based on the information provided by Mohammad Khan. During this, seeing himself surrounded, the accused tried to escape. The police asked him to surrender, but he fired at the police team. Police retaliated, and Aqiluddin was shot in the leg. He was arrested after being injured. According to the police, during the arrest, an illegal .315 bore pistol, one spent cartridge, and one live cartridge were recovered from the possession of the accused. Search for other absconding accused continues SP City Manush Parik stated - The main accused, Aqiluddin, has been arrested after an encounter. He has been sent to the district hospital for treatment. Police teams are continuously raiding to arrest other absconding accused involved in the case. All the accused will be arrested soon.

stories.title: Family feared man who shot father six times:Earlier shot his brother too; marriage proposal turned down
stories.summary: Hari Om Chaudhary (52), a wealthy farmer from Ghaziabad, owned nearly 75 bighas of agricultural land, a commercial market complex, and assets estimated at around Rs 150 crore. Despite the family's financial prosperity, tragedy struck on the night of July 15, when his elder son, Nikhil, allegedly shot him dead. According to police, Nikhil returned home intoxicated around midnight. After being reprimanded by his father for coming home drunk, an argument escalated, and he allegedly fired six rounds at Hari Om with a pistol. Family members say the incident was not an isolated act of violence. In 2018, Nikhil had allegedly shot his younger brother as well, but the family never filed a police complaint, fearing the consequences. This boosted Nikhil's confidence. Why was the family so afraid of Nikhil? Read the inside story… Returned home drunk, opened fire after being scolded On the night of July 15, Hari Om had dinner with his wife, Meenakshi, and younger son, Nishu. Nikhil was out attending a drinking party with friends. He reached home around midnight, where his father objected to his late-night drinking. The verbal argument soon turned into a heated confrontation. As Meenakshi tried to intervene, Nikhil allegedly pulled out a pistol and fired six shots at his father. Hari Om collapsed on the spot after being hit. Mother tried to save husband; younger brother hid in fear Hearing the gunshots, younger son Nishu rushed out of his room. However, upon seeing Nikhil armed with a pistol, he locked himself inside another room, fearing he would be the next target. Meenakshi desperately tried to save her husband, but instead of taking him to hospital, Nikhil fled the scene. Hari Om was later taken to hospital by Meenakshi and Nishu, where doctors declared him dead. Family was arranging his marriage The family had been trying to settle Nikhil through marriage. A marriage proposal from Kankerkhera in Meerut had recently progressed, and both families were initially interested. However, after making inquiries about Nikhil's behaviour in his village, the bride's family decided to withdraw the proposal. The family had since begun searching for another match, believing marriage might help reform him. Earlier shot younger brother, family never complained According to family members, Hari Om had already transferred 25 bighas of farmland to Nikhil for cultivation. He was also allowed to collect rent from the family's commercial market. About a month before the incident, Hari Om had reportedly given Nikhil Rs 40,000 for a trip to Haridwar and Rishikesh. Despite these privileges, relatives say Nikhil's behaviour never improved. They claim his violent temperament had created such fear within the family that no one dared confront him after the 2018 incident, when he allegedly shot his younger brother. Even his parents avoided arguments with him thereafter. Police suspect phone call triggered his anger According to investigators, Meenakshi called Nikhil around 9:30 pm on July 15, asking him to return home because his father was becoming angry. Police said Nikhil, who was drinking with friends at the time, became furious during the call. He allegedly abused his father over the phone and told his mother he would return whenever he wanted. Investigators believe he felt humiliated in front of his friends after receiving the call, and the resentment carried over when he returned home intoxicated later that night. Mother's complaint details the murder In her FIR lodged at Modinagar Police Station, Meenakshi alleged that her husband and son had been arguing over property for a long time. According to the complaint, another argument broke out on the night of July 15 over the same issue. She stated that Nikhil intentionally opened fire on his father and, after Hari Om fell to the ground, fired additional rounds at him in her presence. The bullets struck his head and abdomen. After the shooting, Nikhil allegedly threatened to kill the family before fleeing with the pistol. Victim had also faced a murder allegation Residents of the village claimed that Hari Om Chaudhary's name had surfaced in connection with the 2018 murder of a man named Nain Singh, who belonged to another community. However, according to locals, no FIR was registered in that case, and it was widely believed that the matter was later settled between the two parties, resulting in no legal proceedings.

stories.title: VIDEO | Crocodile attack claims 12-year-old's life:Dragged into river while he went to wash hands; uncle watched helplessly
stories.summary: A horrific incident has been reported from Uttar Pradesh's Bahraich district, where a 12-year-old boy was killed in a crocodile attack. The boy had gone to wash his hands and feet in the Ghaghra river after helping transplant paddy when the crocodile suddenly emerged from the water and clamped him in its jaws. The child struggled to break free, while his uncle and nearby villagers desperately tried to rescue him by throwing bricks and stones at the reptile. However, the crocodile refused to let go, repeatedly dragged the boy underwater and eventually disappeared into deeper water with him. Around five hours later, villagers recovered the child's body from the river. One of his legs and part of his abdomen had been eaten. The incident took place in the Baundi police station area. Station House Officer T.N. Maurya confirmed the incident and the viral video. He said the boy's body was sent for post-mortem on Friday morning. The victim's parents had died a few years ago. He was the only brother to three sisters and was a Class 6 student. See 3 pictures- Boy attacked while washing after working in paddy field According to villagers, Sunil had gone to a paddy field with his uncle, Vijay Raj Singh, at around 2 pm on Thursday to help with paddy transplantation. After working in the field for three to four hours, they stopped at the Ghaghra river while returning home to wash their hands and feet. At that moment, a crocodile suddenly emerged from the water and seized Sunil. Villagers tried to save him with bricks and sticks Sunil's uncle raised the alarm and called out to people working in nearby fields. Villagers rushed to the riverbank and hurled bricks, stones and sticks at the crocodile in an attempt to force it to release the child. Despite their efforts, the reptile held on to the boy, dragged him further into the river and disappeared into deep water. After the attack, more villagers joined the search and used long bamboo poles to look for the child in the river. Body recovered after five-hour search After an extensive search lasting around five hours, villagers recovered Sunil's body from the river. Police said one of his legs and part of his abdomen were missing, indicating the crocodile had partially consumed the body. The body has been sent for a post-mortem examination. Family to receive ₹4 lakh compensation Sub-Divisional Magistrate Prakash Singh said the administration had informed the concerned authorities about the incident. He added that the victim's family would receive ₹4 lakh in financial assistance under the state's disaster relief provisions.

stories.title: Woman's body recovered from a canal near in-laws' home:Married 5 months ago through matrimonial site in Lucknow; sister attempts suicide at police station
stories.summary: The body of a 26-year-old woman, who went missing just five months after her marriage in Lucknow, has been found in a canal around 70 km from her in-laws' home. Her parents alleged that on July 11, their daughter sent a WhatsApp voice message saying, ‘Please take me away from here by 7 am.’ When they reached her in-laws' house the following morning, they found it locked. Her phone, along with those of all her in-laws, had been switched off. Since then, the family had been sitting at Itaunja Police Station seeking action. Meanwhile, on July 13, an unidentified woman's body was recovered from the Salempur Achaka Regulator on the Indira Canal in the Nagaram area. The body remained unidentified until July 16, when the family staged a protest outside the police station. Police then sent the victim's father to the mortuary, where he identified the body as that of his daughter, Himanshi Kashyap. On learning of the identification, Himanshi's mother collapsed at the police station, while her younger sister allegedly attempted self-immolation by pouring diesel on herself. The family accused Himanshi's in-laws of murdering her and alleged that police had failed to act. Himanshi, daughter of Pawan Kashyap from Sitapur, had married Pradeep Gaur of Itaunja five months ago after the match was arranged through a matrimonial website. See 3 pictures- Family accuses police of concealing body's recovery Around 3 pm on Thursday, Himanshi's relatives staged a protest outside Itaunja Police Station, alleging that police had concealed information about the recovery of her body. During the protest, her younger sister, Kirti Kashyap, allegedly attempted self-immolation by pouring petrol on herself. Her brother, Shivraj Kashyap, claimed the family had been waiting at the police station for five days, but officers never informed them that an unidentified woman's body had already been recovered. He alleged that only after the family intensified its protest did police send their father, Pawan Kumar Kashyap, to the mortuary, where he identified Himanshi's body. Newlywed had been missing since July 12 Himanshi Kashyap married Pradeep Gaur, a resident of Turki Mohalla in Itaunja, on February 13. She was originally from Machhli Mandi in Sitapur. According to her family, around midnight on July 12, Himanshi sent a WhatsApp voice message to her younger sister asking her parents to collect her by 7 am. The family alleged that a day earlier, Himanshi had complained to her husband about being assaulted and harassed by her in-laws. When her parents arrived at her matrimonial home on July 12 to take her back, they found the house locked. The phones of Himanshi and all her in-laws were switched off. The family immediately informed police and lodged a complaint. Police awaiting post-mortem report Deputy Commissioner of Police (North) Gopal Krishna Chaudhary said that the preliminary investigation indicated the body recovered from the canal was that of Himanshi Kashyap. He said the family had formally identified the body and that further legal action would be taken after the post-mortem report is received. Father says harassment began within days of marriage Himanshi's father, Pawan Kashyap, runs a tea and samosa stall near Sitapur District Hospital. Speaking earlier at Itaunja Police Station, he said Himanshi was the second of his four children and that her marriage had been arranged through a matrimonial website. He alleged that although the family had spent beyond its means on the wedding, the groom's family continued to demand dowry. According to him, harassment began just 15 days after the marriage. The dispute had previously reached the police station, where a compromise was reached after the in-laws admitted their mistake and assured the family they would treat Himanshi well. Pawan Kashyap now alleges that those assurances were broken and his daughter was killed. He further claimed that CCTV footage from the house captured the victim's brother-in-law, Sandeep Gaur, running towards Himanshi's room carrying a trowel. According to him, the camera stopped recording shortly afterwards. Overcome with emotion while recounting the events, the father broke down and was unable to continue speaking.

stories.title: How to get the cheapest home loan?:Increase eligibility even with low salary; know hidden bank agreement charges
stories.summary: If you're planning to buy a new home and apply for a home loan, careful planning can help you secure a higher loan amount at a lower interest rate, while also saving lakhs of rupees over the loan tenure. Here are the key points every homebuyer should know. Government banks offer the lowest home loan rates Public sector banks are currently offering some of the lowest home loan interest rates. These rates are generally available only to borrowers with a CIBIL score of 750 or above. Banks may charge higher interest rates depending on an applicant's credit profile. How to increase home loan eligibility with a low salary Banks calculate your repayment capacity using the Fixed Obligation to Income Ratio (FOIR). In most cases, they allow 40–50% of your monthly income to be used for EMI payments. For example, if your monthly take-home salary is ₹30,000, the bank may allow an EMI of around ₹15,000. At an interest rate of 7.25% for a 20-year tenure, you may be eligible for a home loan of approximately ₹18.5–19 lakh. If your salary is limiting your loan eligibility, you can improve your chances by: Floating vs Fixed Interest rate: Which is better? More than 95% of home loans in 2026 are being offered at floating interest rates. A floating rate changes according to market conditions and the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) repo rate. A fixed-rate loan remains unchanged throughout the loan period but is usually 1.5% to 3% more expensive than a floating-rate loan. Some fixed-rate loans may also include prepayment penalties. When should you transfer an existing home loan? A home loan balance transfer becomes worthwhile if another bank offers an interest rate at least 1.25 percentage points lower than your current lender. For example, if your existing loan carries an 8.50% interest rate and another bank offers 7.25%, you may consider switching. Experts say a balance transfer is most beneficial within the first five to seven years of the loan, after carefully comparing processing fees, legal charges and other transfer costs. Benefits for first-time homebuyers Eligible first-time buyers may receive an interest subsidy under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY). Tax benefits are also available under the old tax regime: These tax benefits are available only to taxpayers who opt for the old tax regime. Simple ways to reduce your EMI If your EMI feels too high, consider making partial prepayments using bonuses, arrears or any additional income. This reduces the outstanding principal and can either lower your EMI or shorten the loan tenure. If your bank has reduced interest rates for new borrowers, you may also be able to switch your existing loan to the lower rate by paying a switching fee of around 0.25% to 0.50%, reducing your EMI or total interest cost. Check these hidden charges before signing the loan agreement Do not choose a home loan based only on the interest rate. Banks may also charge: Before signing the loan agreement, carefully review all applicable charges to understand the total cost of borrowing.

stories.title: Bulldozers to raze 2 mosques at Jauhar University:Azam Khan says, 'Don't know who built them'; staff claims students no longer visit
stories.summary: 38 of the 40 buildings at former Uttar Pradesh minister and Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan's Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University have been declared unauthorised. The Rampur Development Authority (RDA) has given the university 15 days to remove the structures before initiating demolition. During the process, it also emerged that two mosques inside the campus have been declared unauthorised and are also liable for demolition. Sources associated with the Rampur administration said that during the investigation, the Jauhar Ali Trust was asked about the construction of the mosques. In response, Azam Khan reportedly said, "I do not know who built these mosques." Following Rampur District Magistrate Ajay Kumar Dwivedi's demolition order, only a handful of students reached the university on July 16. By around 3 pm, the campus had fallen silent. Azam Khan's wife, Dr Tanzeen Fatima, arrived at the university at around 2 pm. After finding police personnel deployed inside the premises, she objected and had them removed. Read the full report... 'Faculty and students offer prayers here' The Rampur administration is also investigating the source of funds used to construct various buildings within Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. Two mosques have been built on the campus. One is Umar Mosque, located opposite the Department of Islamic Studies and spread across a large area. The second mosque is situated near the Administrative Block and is visible from a distance. The Rampur Development Authority says permission was never obtained to construct either mosque. In 2019, the Jauhar Ali Trust was asked how the two mosques had been built without approval and where the money for their construction had come from. According to officials, Azam Khan replied that people had come, built the mosques and left. He said faculty members and students now offered prayers there, but the trust did not know who financed or built the structures. With that statement, Azam Khan distanced himself from the construction of the mosques. However, the investigation into the funding used for their construction is still underway. Student numbers fell sharply after Azam Khan's imprisonment Our team visited the university campus. Whether it was discipline or fear of Azam Khan's family, neither students nor faculty members were willing to speak on camera. However, one faculty member, speaking off the record, said there was a time when the university had more than 5,000 students. After Azam Khan was sent to jail, enrolment reportedly dropped to around 1,000-1,200 students. The faculty member added that attendance has fallen even further since the administration issued the demolition order. Student urges government to strengthen the university We spoke to student Sidrul Nisha, who has completed her BSc and returned to seek admission to the MSc Agriculture programme. Asked how she felt about the demolition order for 38 buildings, she said the university had always provided a positive academic environment and a high standard of education. She said Azam Khan had established a good institution that enabled girls to pursue higher education and bring recognition to the district. She described the demolition action as unfair and urged the government to introduce new academic courses and strengthen the university's faculty instead. DM Ajay Kumar Dwivedi explains the demolition order Rampur District Magistrate Ajay Kumar Dwivedi answered questions regarding the notice issued to the university and the action proposed by the authorities. The notice period for Jauhar University has ended. What action will be taken? The university is located in Singan Kheda village, which falls under the jurisdiction of the Rampur Development Authority. A total of 40 buildings have been constructed. Only two have approved building plans, while the remaining 38 were built without permission. Notices were issued to the university. It has submitted a written reply and was also given an opportunity for a personal hearing. It is being claimed that the university was not under the RDA's jurisdiction when it was built. The area has come under the RDA's jurisdiction since 2024. Before that, it was under the Zila Panchayat. The university obtained approval for two buildings from the Zila Panchayat, which clearly shows it was aware of the legal requirements. However, no approval was obtained for the remaining 38 buildings. When will the demolition take place? Under the rules, the institution is given 15 days after the order is issued to remove the unauthorised structures on its own. If this is not done, the Rampur Development Authority will carry out the demolition. 'This is a public road' board installed outside university gate On July 16, the administration installed a signboard directly outside the university entrance stating, "This is a public road." A police team was also deployed near the board. However, a large gate on the road leading into the university remains locked, with Azam Khan's security guards stationed there. No one is allowed to enter the campus without their permission. According to the Public Works Department (PWD), the road passing through the university was built using government funds and is public property. Therefore, the university cannot legally block access to it. Despite the new signboard, another large gate at the far end of the nearly 2-km-long road remains permanently locked. Unless that gate is removed, the road will continue to remain blocked. There had been speculation that the administration would break open the gate on July 16, but no bulldozer was sent. Tanzeen Fatima: 'We have nothing to say at the moment' After receiving information about the police deployment, Dr Tanzeen Fatima arrived at the university on July 16. She asked the police officers at the entrance under whose orders they had come to the university. When they replied that they were acting on directions from senior officials, she responded by asking them to produce an order issued by the university rather than the police. The officers remained silent, after which she asked them to leave the premises. Later, when approached by reporters, Tanzeen Fatima said, “Everyone knows what is happening. We still have 15 days.” Asked whether the university would move the court against the demolition order, she replied, “We cannot say anything at this stage.”

stories.title: Ram Mandir donation theft accused Karunesh was alcoholic:Villagers say he had two marriages and bathed repeatedly after being touched; 'Our village is defamed'
stories.summary: "This is a village of Brahmins. Every household worships Lord Ram, and nothing like this has ever happened before. Overnight, our village has been disgraced. People now call it the 'village of the donation thief.' It has become difficult to walk with our heads held high." Residents of Jayrajpur village, located about 50 km from the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, say this with visible embarrassment. The village is home to Karunesh Pandey, one of the accused in the Ram Mandir donation theft case. Ayodhya Police have recovered ₹18 lakh from Karunesh, claiming the money was siphoned from the temple's donation boxes over time. The Special Investigation Team (SIT) also questioned his father and seized several documents from the family home. Villagers describe Karunesh as an alcoholic whose troubled personal life included two failed marriages and frequent domestic violence. They say his father had been living in Ayodhya to avoid constant family disputes. Villagers say lifestyle never reflected the alleged theft Karunesh belongs to Vashistha Ka Purwa in Jayrajpur village, where nearly 90% of the population belongs to the Brahmin community. When Dainik Bhaskar visited a tea stall near Bariyarpur crossroads, residents were discussing the temple theft. One villager said the family kept to themselves and rarely interacted with others. "His father, Ramdas, works at Khadi Village Industries in Ayodhya and lives there. He used to visit the village only on weekends. Karunesh and his elder brother had earlier worked in Surat." Another resident said the alleged theft had deeply hurt the village's reputation. "This was not an ordinary theft. It was a betrayal of people's faith. No one here is even willing to fight his legal case now because the entire village has been defamed." Despite the alleged theft involving lakhs of rupees, locals said there was no visible change in Karunesh's lifestyle or spending habits. Alcohol addiction, failed marriages and domestic violence Finding Karunesh's house was not easy, as villagers initially hesitated to identify it. Eventually, a local youth led the team there and shared details about his personal life. According to villagers, Karunesh married for the first time about ten years ago. The marriage lasted only three to four years before his wife left him, allegedly because of repeated physical abuse. After she filed a police complaint, Karunesh reportedly paid money as part of a settlement. The couple has a daughter who continues to live in the village. He remarried about five years ago, but villagers claim his behaviour remained unchanged. They allege he frequently consumed excessive alcohol, often passing out in public. Villagers would carry him home. Residents also accused him of regularly assaulting his second wife. "If she cried after being beaten, he would hit her even more and tell her not to let the neighbours hear," one villager claimed. According to locals, his drinking worsened after he started working at the Ram Mandir. Villagers describe him as eccentric A woman from the village described Karunesh as unusually obsessive about cleanliness. "He would wash his motorcycle four or five times a day. Sometimes he even washed his mobile phone. If someone accidentally touched him, he would bathe repeatedly." She said villagers often asked his wife whether he suffered from any medical condition, but she would deny it. Karunesh's elder brothers are locally known by the nicknames Fussan and Mundru. Villagers said Fussan had been working in Surat and later helped Karunesh get a job there. However, Karunesh returned to the village after working for about a year and a half. His father later arranged a job for him through a security agency in Ayodhya. Security agency job led him to the Ram Mandir While working with a security agency in Ayodhya, Karunesh came in contact with another agency—Sainik Security Services Pvt Ltd, based in Varanasi—which supplies security personnel to the Ram Mandir. About a year ago, he was posted at the temple. His responsibility was to transport donation boxes from the temple premises to the counting centre. During this assignment, he became acquainted with Anukalp Mishra, who was responsible for supervising the counting of donations. As both belonged to the same region, they developed a close association. Investigators believe the two later conspired to steal cash from the temple donations. Father says matter is before the court Karunesh's father, Ramdas, has avoided speaking to the media after the arrests. "The matter is before the court now, and the court will decide. We had no idea he had Rs 18 lakh," he said. He also claimed that Karunesh never spent lavishly. “He never even bought biscuits or chocolates for his own children. He never spoke about buying land or jewellery. We are simply maintaining the ancestral property that already belongs to the family.” Police freeze wife's bank account Police said a portion of the recovered Rs 18 lakh had been deposited in Karunesh's wife's bank account, which has now been frozen. When police took Karunesh, Lavkush and Anukalp into custody again on July 8, jewellery was recovered from Anukalp's residence, while Rs 20,000 was reportedly recovered from Karunesh's house. Investigators are still trying to determine whether the accused had plans to invest or hide the stolen money elsewhere. Officials say more details are expected to emerge after the SIT submits its final report.

stories.title: Rain alert in all 75 UP districts:Rivers in spate, rainfall 27% below normal; 2-storey house collapses in Greater Noida
stories.summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh, with thunderstorms and strong winds likely across the state. Monsoon activity has picked up once again, and cloudy skies were seen over Lucknow and nearby districts on Friday morning. Despite the recent rainfall, Uttar Pradesh has received 27% less rainfall than normal since June 1. Rivers swell as rain continues in hill states Continuous rainfall in the Himalayan region has caused the water levels of several rivers in Uttar Pradesh to rise. In Ballia, erosion has started along the banks of the Ghaghara River. In the Bansdih area, residents have begun demolishing their own permanent houses and relocating to safer places. Around 150 families have already left their homes. In Varanasi, rising water levels in the Ganga River have submerged the steps of the Dashashwamedh Ghat. However, the river is still 11.90 metres below the danger mark. In Mathura, the Yamuna River is in spate and flowing 1.30 metres below the warning level. The steps of Keshi Ghat in Vrindavan have also been submerged. In Prayagraj, water from the Ganga and Yamuna has reached shops built along the ghats. See 4 pictures- Rainfall still 27% below normal According to the weather department, Uttar Pradesh has recorded 27% below-normal rainfall so far this monsoon season. During the past 24 hours, 25 cities received rainfall, with Lakhimpur Kheri recording the highest rainfall at 22.5 mm. Rain-related incidents across the state Heavy rain and strong winds caused several incidents across Uttar Pradesh on Thursday. Two-storey house collapses in Greater Noida A two-storey house collapsed in Tilpata village of Greater Noida at around 1:30 pm on Thursday. The house was located beside a drain, and its foundation reportedly weakened due to continuous rainfall. Fortunately, no casualties were reported. Monsoon expected to become more active Senior meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh from Lucknow said a weather system is currently active over eastern Uttar Pradesh, while the monsoon trough is passing through the Terai region. He said cloud cover is present across the state, but widespread rainfall has not yet occurred. Meanwhile, the low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal is strengthening and is expected to move northwest over the next 48 hours. According to the IMD, the monsoon is expected to become more active across Uttar Pradesh after July 17, bringing more widespread and heavier rainfall.

stories.title: Video | CM Yadav inspects Simhastha works on bike:Wears helmet, walks 2 km through Ujjain, makes jalebis during ground reality check
stories.summary: Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav conducted an on-ground inspection of preparations for Simhastha-2028 on Friday evening, setting aside official protocol to tour parts of Ujjain on a motorcycle while wearing a helmet. The Chief Minister later walked nearly 2 kilometres through the city to review ongoing development works, interacted with residents, and issued on-the-spot instructions to officials. During the visit, he also stopped at a familiar sweet shop at Kanthal Square, where he prepared jalebis and shared tea with the shop owner. Motorcycle tour across key development sites After arriving in Ujjain from Nagda on Friday evening, CM Yadav left the Chief Minister's residence on a motorcycle wearing a helmet. He inspected ongoing infrastructure and development projects across several locations, including: The inspection focused on works related to preparations for Simhastha-2028, one of the country's largest religious congregations. See these pictures Walks 2 km, interacts with residents After reviewing construction work at Freeganj Bridge and Medicity, the Chief Minister walked nearly 2 kilometres from Koyla Phatak to Kanthal Square. During the walk, he assessed road widening projects and other Simhastha-related infrastructure works, interacted with local residents, and issued directions to officials to expedite pending work. Residents welcomed him at several points along the route. Stops at old acquaintance's sweet shop At Kanthal Square, the Chief Minister visited a jalebi shop owned by an old acquaintance. He prepared jalebis himself, ordered tea, and drank warm water while interacting with the shop owner. Yadav said he had been associated with the shop since his days in student politics. 'Wanted to see the ground reality myself' Speaking to the media, the Chief Minister said preparations for Simhastha-2028 are progressing rapidly. He said the state government is strengthening roads, traffic management, and civic infrastructure to accommodate the expected influx of millions of devotees during the religious event. Explaining his decision to inspect the city on a motorcycle and on foot, Yadav said the objective was to personally assess the actual progress of development works on the ground. He also noted that after the development of the Mahakal Mahalok corridor, religious tourism in Ujjain has increased significantly, contributing to the state's economy and creating more employment opportunities.

stories.title: Google alert leads to man's arrest for recording obscene clips:Police say accused secretly filmed minor girls' private moments
stories.summary: A man has been arrested in Kanpur in a child sexual abuse material (CSAM) case after Google alerted the police about suspected illegal content stored on his Google Drive. According to police, the accused allegedly secretly recorded explicit videos of his minor cousins and other girls from his neighbourhood, uploaded the files to Google Drive, and stored them there. Following a digital alert received from Google, police tracked him using his IMEI number and IP address. The accused was arrested on Friday, and police said 15 objectionable videos involving minor girls were recovered from his phone and cloud storage. Investigators are also examining whether any of the videos were shared or uploaded to other online platforms. The case falls under the Chaman Ganj police station limits in Kanpur. Google alert triggered investigation Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police (Crime) Anjali Vishwakarma said the Cyber Crime Police Station received information on July 6 through the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP) regarding a serious offence involving women and children. Following the alert, two cyber investigation teams launched a confidential probe. Google shared digital information related to the account, enabling investigators to identify the suspect and proceed with the investigation. Accused traced through digital evidence Police said Google provided several technical details, including: Using this information, investigators identified and arrested the accused from the Chaman Ganj area. According to police, the accused is a high school graduate who works in the baby diaper business. Investigators said he had deleted the videos from his mobile phone but stored them in Google Drive, where Google's automated safety systems flagged the content. During questioning, the accused allegedly admitted that he had been secretly recording videos for the past three months. Videos allegedly included minor family members Police alleged that the accused secretly recorded explicit videos of: Some videos were allegedly recorded without the victims' knowledge, including while they were in private spaces. Police said around 15 objectionable videos have been recovered so far. Investigators also revealed that the National Center for Missing Exploited Children (NCMEC) had generated four cyber tipline reports related to the accused's account. During the investigation, police also found information linked to three additional complaints. Police investigating possible online distribution Police are now examining whether the recovered videos were merely stored in cloud storage or were also uploaded or distributed through other websites or online platforms. Digital forensic analysis of the accused's devices and online accounts is currently underway. How Google detects such content Police explained that many users store personal files on Google Drive, but the platform also uses automated safety systems and technical tools to identify content that violates its policies. If uploaded files are detected as suspected Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) or other prohibited content, Google's systems may flag the account. In accordance with legal requirements, Google may share relevant information with law enforcement agencies, including: This information helps investigators identify suspects and pursue criminal cases. Content prohibited on Google Drive Under Google's policies and applicable law, users are prohibited from storing or sharing content such as: The investigation is ongoing, and police are continuing to examine the accused's digital activity to determine the full extent of the alleged offences.

stories.title: Lucknow City Health Officer takes charge:Focuses on waterlogging and communicable disease control, reviews preparedness with sanitation and food officials
stories.summary: Newly appointed Municipal Health Officer (MHO) Ashish Kumar Singh on Friday formally assumed charge at the Lucknow Municipal Corporation headquarters and held his first review meeting with Zonal Sanitary Officers (ZSOs) and Sanitary and Food Inspectors (SFIs). During the meeting, Singh instructed officials to carry out their responsibilities with seriousness and accountability. He reviewed key civic issues, including sanitation, waterlogging, communicable disease control, fogging operations, drainage maintenance, and disposal of public grievances. Special monitoring of waterlogging-prone areas The Municipal Health Officer sought detailed information on identified waterlogging hotspots across the city. He directed officials to maintain close surveillance in vulnerable areas and ensure immediate response during heavy rainfall. Field officers were also instructed to regularly monitor ground conditions and promptly report updates to senior authorities. Warning for unauthorised absence Emphasising accountability, Singh instructed officials to issue warnings to employees found absent without valid justification. He also directed supervisory officers to closely monitor the attendance and performance of staff working under their jurisdiction. Daily field inspections made mandatory All Zonal Sanitary Officers and Sanitary Food Inspectors have been instructed to conduct daily field inspections in their respective areas. The Municipal Health Officer stressed that the actual condition of sanitation services can only be assessed through on-site inspections rather than office-based reviews. Any deficiencies identified during inspections must be rectified without delay. Accelerate communicable disease control campaign Reviewing the city's communicable disease prevention campaign, Singh directed officials to intensify operations, particularly in identified disease hotspots. He asked officials to ensure daily action in vulnerable areas and submit regular reports on progress to facilitate effective monitoring. Coordination on drainage issues The meeting also discussed problems related to major drains across the city. Singh instructed officials that issues falling outside the Health Department's jurisdiction should immediately be referred to the concerned departments. Any open drains or drainage-related hazards must be reported without delay so corrective action can be initiated. Officials' concerns heard The Municipal Health Officer also interacted with Zonal Sanitary Officers and Food Inspectors to understand operational challenges faced during fieldwork. He assured them that practical issues affecting their work would be addressed through appropriate administrative measures. He further directed that a meeting with agencies responsible for sanitation services be held within the next week to strengthen accountability and improve cleanliness across the city. Regular fogging across all zones Officials have been instructed to carry out fogging operations regularly based on local requirements. Singh said that any shortage of fogging machines, fuel or other resources should be resolved immediately in coordination with the concerned agencies to ensure uninterrupted operations. He also directed all implementing agencies to maintain adequate manpower, equipment and other resources so that sanitation work is not affected. Time-bound disposal of public complaints The Municipal Health Officer instructed officials to ensure 100% time-bound disposal of all complaints related to sanitation, waterlogging, fogging and public health received through any platform. He also directed that details of action taken and complaint resolution must be promptly shared with the municipal war room to ensure continuous monitoring and accountability.

stories.title: UP's district panchayat chiefs become administrators for first time:Government bars them from taking major decisions as appointments await High Court ruling
stories.summary: In a first for Uttar Pradesh, the Yogi Adityanath government has appointed the existing chairpersons of all 75 district Panchayats as administrators after the completion of their constitutional tenure, allowing them to continue in office until fresh panchayat elections are held. The official order was issued on Friday, a day before the current tenure of all district panchayat chairpersons ends on July 11. Ordinarily, after the expiry of a district panchayat's term, the District Magistrate (DM) is appointed as administrator. However, under the new order, the elected chairpersons will remain in charge in an administrative capacity. Panchayati Raj Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar confirmed that the government has formally entrusted the district panchayat chairpersons with the role of administrators. No Major Policy Decisions, Routine Administration to Continue Although the chairpersons will continue to head their respective district panchayats, the government has imposed certain restrictions on their powers to avoid legal and procedural complications. As administrators, they will not be permitted to take major policy decisions, but they will continue to oversee: Official work will continue under their signatures until the newly elected bodies assume office. First such decision in Uttar Pradesh This is the first time in Uttar Pradesh that elected district panchayat chairpersons have been appointed as administrators after the expiry of their constitutional term instead of handing over charge to bureaucrats. The move comes as panchayat elections in the state have been delayed due to pending legal proceedings. Government's strategic objectives The decision is widely seen as serving multiple administrative and political objectives. BJP retains administrative presence in most districts Of the state's 75 district panchayats, 68 are currently headed by BJP-backed chairpersons, allowing the ruling party to retain its presence in district-level governance until elections are held. Avoiding complete bureaucratic control Had District Magistrates been appointed as administrators, elected representatives would have had no role in district panchayat administration. The new arrangement ensures that existing chairpersons continue to function as local administrative heads. Maintaining organisational strength ahead of elections With the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections approaching, the continuation of district panchayat chairpersons is expected to help the ruling party maintain its organisational network and outreach in rural areas. Why the government took this decision According to the government, the move was intended to: What happens next? The new administrative arrangement will take effect immediately after the chairpersons' tenure expires on July 11. Meanwhile, the issue remains under judicial scrutiny. The government's earlier decision to appoint gram pradhans as administrators has already been challenged before the Allahabad High Court, with the next hearing scheduled for July 13. The High Court's observations in that case could have implications for the district panchayat arrangement as well.

stories.title: Rajbhar blames Akhilesh for Panchayat poll delay:Minister says, 'Govt was ready for elections'; claims 'Islam teaches hatred'
stories.summary: Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) chief and Uttar Pradesh Cabinet Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar blamed the Samajwadi Party (SP) for the delay in the state's Panchayat elections, alleging that legal action initiated by the party stalled the poll process. Addressing the media on Friday in Ambedkar Nagar at 2 pm, Rajbhar claimed the Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath-led government had completed all preparations to conduct the elections on time. "The Panchayati Raj Department had completed all necessary preparations and procedures. We were ready to conduct the elections, but a petition filed by Akhilesh Yadav's legal cell advisor in the High Court delayed the process," he said. 'Government was prepared, court case delayed polls' Rajbhar said the Allahabad High Court subsequently summoned both the Uttar Pradesh government and the State Election Commission after the petition was filed. According to him, the government submitted timely responses to all the court's queries and remains prepared to hold the elections once legal issues are resolved. High Court to hear matter again on July 13 The minister said that, following earlier directions from the High Court, the government had constituted a Backward Classes Commission to comply with legal requirements related to panchayat elections. He added that after administrators were appointed in place of village heads (Gram Pradhans), objections were raised against that decision as well. Rajbhar said the High Court has now summoned the government again on July 13, seeking an explanation for appointing administrators in place of elected village heads. "The ball is now entirely in the High Court's court. Whatever directions the court gives after the July 13 hearing, the government will act accordingly," he said. Remarks on Sanatan and Islam Rajbhar also made remarks comparing Sanatan Dharma and Islam. He said Sanatan Dharma promotes brotherhood, harmony and social unity, while alleging that Islam teaches hatred. He further accused Akhilesh Yadav of previously practising "politics centred around Islam" and claimed that the SP leader has recently begun speaking about Sanatan Dharma because of changing political circumstances. Fresh attack on Akhilesh Yadav Continuing his criticism of the Samajwadi Party chief, Rajbhar repeated an earlier allegation that party workers had told him money was demanded from people seeking to meet Akhilesh Yadav. He said he had earlier posted about the allegation on social media platform X after receiving complaints. Comments on socialism and PDA Referring to socialist leader Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia, Rajbhar said a "true socialist" does not use caste identifiers with his or her name. He questioned why Akhilesh Yadav continues to use a caste surname if he truly believes in socialist principles. The minister also criticised the Samajwadi Party's PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) political plank, alleging that its leaders frequently change the meaning of the acronym and make inconsistent statements. Criticism of previous Samajwadi governments Rajbhar also accused previous Samajwadi Party governments in Uttar Pradesh of fostering an atmosphere of lawlessness, alleging that their tenures were marked by incidents of crime, looting and murder. The Panchayat election matter remains pending before the Allahabad High Court, with the next hearing scheduled for July 13.

stories.title: Grandfather dies saving grandson from electrocution:Child's iron rod touched high-tension line as he tried to retrieve kite
stories.summary: A 65-year-old man died of electrocution while trying to save his 12-year-old grandson, who came into contact with an 11,000-volt high-tension power line while attempting to retrieve a kite from an electricity pole using an iron rod. The incident occurred around 12 pm on Friday in the Khurja area of Bulandshahr. The injured boy is undergoing treatment at a higher medical centre. A video of the incident has also surfaced. Kite got stuck in electricity pole According to police, Ahad (12) had gone to his grandfather's house in Burj Usman village to play. While flying a kite on the rooftop, the kite became entangled in an electricity pole carrying an 11 kV high-tension line. The boy attempted to retrieve it using an iron rod, which came into contact with the power line. The current passed through the rod, electrocuting him. Witnesses said sparks and smoke erupted from the pole as the child caught fire and began screaming in pain. First 2 pictures Grandfather dies while trying to save him Seeing his grandson in distress, Israr (65) rushed to rescue him. He tried to pull the boy away with his bare hands, but was himself struck by the powerful electric current. The child was thrown away from the point of contact, while Israr collapsed unconscious. Family members rushed both of them to the hospital. Doctors declared Israr dead on arrival, while Ahad, who suffered critical injuries, was referred to a higher medical facility, where he remains under treatment. Police confirm electrocution Khurja Station House Officer Ramphal Singh said the elderly man died while trying to save the child after he came into contact with the high-voltage line. Police have sent the body for post-mortem examination. Further action will be taken after the report is received, the officer said. Family background Ahad's father, Abrar (35), works at a pottery manufacturing unit. The family lives in Burj Usman village. Ahad studies in Class 3 at a private school and has two younger siblings. According to the family, he had gone to visit his grandfather when the fatal accident occurred.

stories.title: Fake MLM racket busted, 300 job seekers rescued:₹50 lakh extorted through bogus network marketing scheme; 19 arrested
stories.summary: Varanasi Police have busted a large-scale fake multi-level marketing (MLM) and pyramid scheme, rescuing around 300 unemployed youths who were allegedly confined and pressured to recruit more people into the network after paying hefty registration fees. The operation was carried out on Thursday after police raided a three-storey building in the Rohania police station area. Following interrogation, 19 people were arrested in connection with the racket. Police also seized 20 mobile phones and two luxury cars from the accused. Victims lured with fake job offers DCP (Crime) Neetu Kadyan said the gang was operating under the guise of a corporate office and running an illegal MLM and pyramid marketing network. The accused allegedly contacted unemployed youths from Bihar, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and other states, offering office jobs, Tata company jobs and agricultural work with a promised salary of ₹25,000 per month. After being brought to Varanasi, the victims were made to attend fake interviews in what appeared to be a corporate office. They were then asked to pay ₹30,000–35,000 as registration or joining fees. In return, they were handed a basic kit containing low-value items such as clothes, oil and soap worth only ₹1,000–2,000. Brainwashed into expanding the network According to police, the victims were subsequently shifted to a training centre where they were allegedly subjected to psychological manipulation. The recruits were promised a luxurious lifestyle and pressured to bring at least three new members into the network. They were allegedly threatened that if they failed to recruit others, they would neither receive salaries nor get refunds of the money they had paid. Gang operated through fake companies Police said the accused were operating under a fake company named Mahadev Enterprises and had obtained a franchise of an MLM firm called Royal Health Wellness Private Limited to lend legitimacy to their activities. The operation allegedly functioned as an organised cyber-enabled recruitment fraud targeting unemployed youth across multiple states. Gang leader identified, financial probe underway ACP (Crime) Vidush Saxena identified the alleged kingpin as Deepak Kumar Shah, a resident of Jamui district in Bihar. Police said preliminary examination of his State Bank of India (SBI) and HDFC Bank accounts revealed around ₹4 crore in credits over the past year. Investigators also found: Police said a detailed financial investigation is underway to determine the full scale of the racket. 19 arrested Police arrested the following accused: Police said further investigation is in progress to identify additional victims, trace the money trail and determine whether more people were involved in operating the network.

stories.summary: Anandiben Patel – उत्तरप्रदेश की गवर्नर आनंदीबेन पटेल के एक बयान पर बवाल मच गया है। उन्होंने एक कार्यक्रम में प्रेम विवाह, भागते प्रेमी जोड़ों और पढ़ाई के दौरान युवतियों की प्रेग्नेंसी पर कमेंट किए। गवर्नर आनंदीबेन पटेल का कार्यक्रम का यह वीडियो वायरल हो गया जिससे पॉलिटिकल विवाद खड़ा हो गया है। सोशल मीडिया में उनके बयान पर तीखी प्रतिक्रिया व्यक्त की जा रही है। गवर्नर आनंदीबेन पटेल के कमेंट्स, उत्तरप्रदेश सहित देशभर में पॉलिटिकल सर्कल के बीच बहस का विषय बन गए हैं। आलोचकों का कहना है कि उन्होंने जिस एकेडमिक इवेंट में ये बातें कहीं, वह कार्यक्रम स्टूडेंट्स की अचीवमेंट को सेलिब्रेट करने के लिए रखा गया था। कांग्रेस के वरिष्ठ नेता टीएस सिंह देव ने कहा कि, “यह बालिग़ पुरुषों और महिलाओं के बीच के रिश्तों का मामला है। मेरी राय में, सामाजिक ढांचे के भीतर, आम तौर पर शादी के बाद ही गर्भधारण होना चाहिए। गर्भवती होना एक बात है, लेकिन पैदा होने वाले बच्चे को सामाजिक माहौल में अलग नज़रिए से देखा जाएगा।” लगातार हो रही आलोचना के बाद गर्वनर आनंदीबेन पटेल ने सफाई भी दी। उन्होंने स्पष्ट किया कि उनका मकसद लव मैरिज का विरोध करना नहीं था।

stories.title: Gorakhpur District Hospital launches Dengue prevention campaign:Health dept on alert amid monsoon, urges weekly 'Dry Day'
stories.summary: With the risk of dengue expected to rise during the monsoon season, the Gorakhpur Health Department has stepped up preventive measures across the city. As part of the initiative, a special Dengue Prevention Drive was conducted at the District Hospital campus on Thursday at 2 PM. During the campaign, extensive cleanliness activities were carried out within the hospital premises and surrounding areas. Waterlogging spots were identified, anti-larval chemicals were sprayed, and people were educated about measures to prevent dengue. Multi-department campaign led by senior health officials The drive was conducted under the leadership of Chief Medical Officer (CMO) Dr Rajesh Jha and Chief Medical Superintendent Dr OP Singh. Teams from the Health Department, Malaria Department, Filaria Department, and the Municipal Corporation jointly participated in the operation. Accumulated water found inside the hospital campus was immediately removed, while anti-larval treatment was carried out at locations prone to mosquito breeding. Healthcare workers and hospital staff were also sensitised about dengue prevention measures. Dengue mosquito breeds in clean, stagnant water: CMO According to the CMO Dr Rajesh Jha, the Aedes mosquito, which transmits dengue, breeds rapidly in clean and stagnant water. He urged residents to ensure that water does not collect in their homes, on rooftops, or in surrounding areas. And stressed that awareness and preventive precautions are more effective than medicines in controlling the spread of dengue. Residents urged to observe a weekly 'Dry Day' District Malaria Officer Angad Singh appealed to residents to observe a 'Dry Day' at least once every week. He advised people to completely empty and clean coolers, flower pots, refrigerator trays, overhead water tanks, buckets, and other water storage containers once a week. According to him, this simple practice prevents mosquito breeding and significantly reduces the risk of dengue transmission. Anti-dengue campaigns to continue across the district The campaign was attended by Medical Superintendent Dr BK Suman, Senior Consultant Dr Rajesh, Quality Manager Dr Mukul, along with doctors, healthcare workers, and teams from the Municipal Corporation, Malaria Department, and Filaria Department. Officials said that, in addition to the ongoing "Dengue-Free Hostel Campaign," similar dengue prevention drives will continue at hospitals, government institutions, and other public places across the district to protect people from mosquito-borne diseases during the rainy season.

stories.title: Man gets death sentence for killing 1.5-year-old boy:Convict pressured child's mother to marry him; slammed toddler to ground 8 times
stories.summary: A court in Firozabad has sentenced a man to death for the brutal murder of an 18-month-old boy, whom he allegedly killed after the child's mother rejected his repeated marriage proposal. The verdict was delivered on Friday at 2:45 pm, nearly one month and 10 days after the crime. The child was murdered in Shikohabad on 30, and CCTV footage of the incident had also surfaced. It showed the accused killing the child. Police later arrested the accused after shooting him in both legs. Court delivers verdict in just over a month Government counsel Rajeev Priyadarshi said the court pronounced its judgment within one month and 10 days of the incident. Police filed the chargesheet within six days of the murder. During the trial, the defence argued that the accused was mentally unstable at the time of the incident. However, the court rejected the claim and held Viraj alias Jitendra Pathak guilty. According to the prosecutor, CCTV footage proved to be the most critical piece of evidence. When the footage was played in court, the accused reportedly began slapping himself and appeared visibly distressed. The prosecution said the speedy conviction would strengthen public confidence in the justice system. Background: Marriage proposal rejected According to police and the victim's family, the child's mother, Rati Sharma, had married Suneet, a resident of Badaun, about three years ago. However, the couple had been facing marital disputes, and Rati had been staying with her mother. The accused, Viraj, who is the son of Suneet's aunt from Shekhupur in Badaun, had allegedly been pressuring Rati to marry him despite knowing she was already married. Her family said she repeatedly rejected his proposal, after which he became angry. Toddler lured away on the pretext of buying candy On May 30, Rati had gone with her mother, daughter and her 18-month-old son Aarav to visit a friend, Pushplata Pathak, who had recently been injured in a road accident. Viraj also arrived at the house that afternoon. According to investigators, he took Aarav away on the pretext of buying him candy. After reaching a deserted lane, he allegedly smashed the child onto the ground eight times, causing fatal head injuries. He later returned carrying the unconscious child, left him outside the house and fled. Family members rushed Aarav to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. CCTV captured the murder Police examined CCTV cameras installed near the crime scene, which allegedly showed the accused repeatedly throwing the child onto the ground. The footage became the prosecution's strongest evidence during the trial. Following the incident, police tracked down the accused. During an alleged encounter, he sustained bullet injuries to both legs before being arrested. Mother says, 'My child's neck was hanging' Rati said, "My in-laws used to assault me, and I was often unwell. Because of this, my mother brought me back to live with her. After some time, Viraj, the son of my husband's aunt, started calling me. One day, he said he was coming to meet me and proposed marriage. I refused, telling him I was already married and had a child." "Viraj came to my aunt's house and took my son Aarav with him on the pretext of buying him a toffee. Since he was a relative, I had no reason to suspect him." She alleged that Viraj took Aarav a short distance away and repeatedly slammed him to the ground, killing him. "My child's neck was completely limp," she said. According to police, the accused allegedly slammed the child onto the ground eight times, causing fatal head injuries. He then carried Aarav back in his arms, left him outside the house, and fled. When family members found the child, they rushed him to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Police later examined CCTV footage from the area, which allegedly showed Viraj assaulting the child. He was subsequently arrested after police shot him in both legs during an encounter. Speedy investigation led to conviction District Government Counsel Rajeev Priyadarshi said the police and prosecution pursued the case swiftly. The prosecution completed the examination of 13 witnesses in a short period, and the court convicted the accused based on strong eyewitness testimony, forensic evidence and the CCTV footage. The court ultimately awarded the death penalty for what it considered a rare and brutal crime.
