The Trinamool Congress and Bharatiya Janata Party both voiced their strong opinions regarding her visit. Exiled since 2007, Nasreen is set to participate in an anti-fundamentalism literary event this August. Her previous works and the circumstances of her exile have sent shockwaves through conversations about free speech and the intersection with religious beliefs in West Bengal.

stories.title: 6 most snake-filled water bodies in South Carolina: From the Savannah River to the ACE Basin
stories.summary: South Carolina's abundant waters attract many snake species, both harmless and dangerous. The Savannah River and Great Pee Dee River are home to several notable snake populations. Congaree River and Lake Murray host a variety of snakes, including venomous ones. Lake Hartwell and the ACE Basin also feature numerous water-dwelling snake species. These warm environments and plentiful prey make South Carolina ideal for snakes.

stories.title: How tiny pollen grains helped solve a brutal murder: The fascinating science behind nature's invisible crime scene evidence
stories.summary: Tiny pollen grains offer vital clues for investigators solving complex criminal cases. Forensic palynologists analyze these microscopic particles to link suspects to crime scenes. A notable murder case in New Zealand was solved using unusual mutated pollen evidence. Pollen's resistance to decomposition makes it a persistent and valuable forensic tool. This silent evidence helps identify and locate regions, aiding in criminal investigations.

stories.title: New highway hurt his town. At 98, he helped revive America's famous Route 66
In Tokyo's hidden 1,100-year-old shrine, thousands of desperate fans are praying for impossible concert tickets
Florida treasure hunters searching a 400-year-old shipwreck discovered a rare 22.5-pound silver bar worth up to $100,000

Quote of the day by Stoic philosopher Epictetus: "Any person capable of angering you becomes your master; he can anger you only when…" - why losing control of your emotions can hand power to someone else
stories.summary: Stoic philosopher Epictetus taught that anger is a choice, not an automatic reaction. He believed individuals control their responses to external provocations. This ancient wisdom remains relevant in today's digital age. Modern life offers many opportunities for emotional entanglement with others. Recognizing this power dynamic helps maintain personal control over one's day.

stories.title: Scientists fitted a European honey buzzard with a GPS tracker. The bird flew for 42 days, covering more than 10,000 km from South Africa to Finland and helping researchers uncover the secrets of one of nature's greatest migrations
China's Brahmaputra mega dam: Can it control river water flowing into India?
stories.summary: China is constructing a massive hydropower project on the Yarlung Tsangpo River. This project raises significant water security and strategic concerns for India. Experts warn of potential impacts on downstream water flows and ecological stability. India is accelerating its own hydropower development in response to these developments. The project's long-term implications for regional water management remain under scrutiny.

stories.title: NCP reunification on cards? CM Fadnavis' talks with leaders of both factions fuels buzz
'May die in 2 days, lost 8.5 kg': Plea in Delhi HC seeks 'force-feeding' of Sonam Wangchuk as hunger strike takes toll on activist's health
stories.summary: A plea seeks court intervention to force-feed activist Sonam Wangchuk, whose hunger strike has entered its eighteenth day. Concerns are growing over his deteriorating health as he has reportedly lost significant weight. The petition urges authorities to shift him to a government hospital for medical intervention. It argues that saving his life is of paramount importance for the nation.

stories.title: Nepal court jails ex-deputy PM, home minister in fake refugee scam; 14 others convicted
stories.summary: Two former Nepal ministers received prison sentences for their involvement in a fake refugee document scam. Top Bahadur Rayamajhi was sentenced to four years, and Bal Krishna Khand received two years. Fourteen others were also convicted and sentenced for their roles in the alleged fraud. The investigation began in 2023 after authorities uncovered claims of Nepali citizens posing as refugees.

stories.title: AI wants more than your searches now
stories.summary: Internet and social media giants are looking to track how you engage with their services as they seek to improve their AI models. Here’s what you need to know

stories.title: 'Received nothing but silence': CJP's Dipke slams Centre as Sonam Wangchuk's fast enters Day 18
stories.summary: Abhijeet Dipke criticized the government's silence regarding Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike. Wangchuk has been fasting for eighteen days protesting examination irregularities and paper leaks. He questioned why the Prime Minister has not engaged in dialogue. Opposition leaders have appealed to Wangchuk to end his fast due to his health. Wangchuk has lost 8.5 kg since beginning his protest on June 28.

stories.title: Middle East war: Trump weighs 'devastating strikes'; Iran targets US bases in Middle East - key points
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard has asserted that the Strait of Hormuz will stay closed until the United States changes its course of action. This comes on the heels of the US conducting new strikes near the Strait and reinstating a naval blockade. Iran has also announced attacks on US bases in Kuwait and Bahrain, exacerbating regional tensions after a recently collapsed truce.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Princess Diana: "I don't want expensive gifts; I don't want to be bought. I have everything I want. I just want someone to…" - why emotional security can matter more than wealth or luxury
stories.summary: Princess Diana emphasized that emotional security surpasses material possessions. She desired dependable presence and a feeling of safety from loved ones. This need for reassurance begins in childhood and continues throughout life. Genuine presence offers more to relationships than grand, extravagant gestures. Her words highlight the enduring human need for emotional connection and support.

stories.title: 'If she publicly says ...': Congress extends Martyrs' Day invite to Mamata, but with a condition
stories.summary: The Congress invited Mamata Banerjee to its Martyrs' Day event in Kolkata. This invitation came with a condition that she acknowledge leaving Congress was a mistake. West Bengal Congress president stated Mamata should not distort the historical significance of the 1993 movement. He added that admitting her past decision was wrong would be a significant gesture. The Congress stage remains open for her to pay respects to the martyrs.

stories.title: FBI adds Indian-origin man to most wanted list over alleged organised crime links
stories.summary: The FBI has added Nitish Kaushal to its most wanted list for his alleged role in organized crime. Kaushal is linked to the Jaggu Bhagwanpuria group involved in various illegal activities. This action follows charges against Lawrence Bishnoi and Goldy Brar for a Canadian assassination. Federal agents recently conducted large raids targeting the Lawrence Bishnoi network in the United States.

stories.title: US seismologist has been detained in China for nearly 2 years without trial: Family
stories.summary: A Chinese-born American seismologist faces spying charges in China. Youlin Chen has been detained for nearly two years, according to his wife. US officials have designated his detention as wrongful and a top priority. China denies any wrongful detention and states its judicial organs follow law. The case adds tension to the ongoing relationship between the two nuclear-armed nations.

stories.title: Where Indians come to watch, and be watched
stories.summary: From Shubman Gill and Priyanka Chopra to tennis lifers such as Lara Dutta and Ravi Shastri, Wimbledon now offers sport, style, status, and sentiment

stories.title: Cuss remarks against CJI: Two law students arrested over courtroom disruption
Boat tragedy in San Francisco: One dead, two missing after pontoon boat capsizes near Alcatraz
Thailand scraps plan to end visa-free entry for Indians
stories.summary: Thailand will now allow thirty-day visa-exempt entries for Indian visitors. This decision follows a recent drop in arrivals from India impacting tourism. The government aims to align with Indian tourist travel behavior and boost visitor numbers. Previously, Indian tourists enjoyed sixty days visa-free entry to the country. This change reverses an earlier proposal to eliminate visa-free access for many nations.

stories.title: ADAG companies siphoned off loan money via 53 shell firms: ED
stories.summary: Enforcement Directorate informed the Supreme Court about Reliance ADAG entities siphoning funds. These companies allegedly used fifty-three shell entities to divert bank loans. Assets worth over Rs 5,500 crore have been attached by the agency. Other Reliance group companies also diverted funds for luxury acquisitions. Investigations continue with significant assets attached and officials arrested.

stories.title: Supreme Court acquits man, 16 others in 26-year-old dowry case
stories.summary: The Supreme Court acquitted seventeen individuals accused in a dowry death case. This decision came after a lengthy twenty-six-year legal battle for the family. The court criticized lower courts for disregarding defense evidence without valid reasons. Substantive testimonies and credible documents presented by the defense remained uncontroverted. The apex court stressed the importance of treating all evidence equally during trials.

stories.title: Ahead of Lok Sabha session, Birla may recognise rebel TMC MPs' merger with NCPI
stories.summary: Rebel TMC MPs are set to hold their parliamentary party meeting under NCPI. They anticipate representation at the customary pre-session all-party meeting. Speaker Om Birla will decide on merger applications before the monsoon session begins. Recognition of NCPI could make it BJP's largest ally in the Lok Sabha. The rebel group is confident of approval due to their numbers.

stories.title: NCPI plans MPs meeting as Birla likely to decide on its recognition plea before session
stories.summary: Rebel TMC MPs are set to hold their parliamentary party meeting under NCPI. They anticipate representation at the customary pre-session all-party meeting. Speaker Om Birla will decide on merger applications before the monsoon session begins. Recognition of NCPI could make it BJP's largest ally in the Lok Sabha. The rebel group is confident of approval due to their numbers.

stories.title: Supreme Court fines Raina, 4 others Rs 3 lakh each for taking court for ride
stories.summary: The Supreme Court imposed a three lakh rupee cost on Samay Raina and four others. These comedians failed to hold a promised show for disabled individuals. They had previously faced court anger for mocking people with disabilities. The court accused Raina of lying and taking the judiciary for a ride. The bench warned artists against disrespecting people with disabilities and their talents.

stories.title: SOP soon to hear petitions after working hours, says Supreme Court
stories.summary: The Supreme Court will create a procedure for urgent petitions. This new system will address life and liberty concerns after court hours. The court agreed to explore this after a lawyer's plea for immediate access. Only cases involving life and liberty infringements will be considered. This aims to provide prompt constitutional protection to citizens.

stories.title: This man arrived at a Paris airport expecting to catch a flight. Instead, he lived there for the next 18 years
"Dumb disgusting low IQ animal": Hasan Piker's explosive Clavicular praise turns into brutal Asmongold attack
stories.summary: Hasan Piker has sparked fresh controversy after praising Clavicular for avoiding political commentary while launching a scathing attack on fellow streamer Asmongold. During a livestream, Hasan accused Asmongold of speaking on issues he does not understand and used harsh insults against him. A viral X post amplified the remarks, igniting heated debate over influencers discussing politics and their responsibility to large audiences.

stories.title: Madhya Pradesh's UCC draft proposes registration of live-in couples
stories.summary: Madhya Pradesh's draft uniform civil code requires live-in relationship registration. Couples must formally cancel registrations when relationships end, facing penalties for non-compliance. Parents will be informed of their children's live-in relationship status. Inheritance laws will change, including fathers as heirs to deceased sons' property. The proposed code will initially exclude the state's tribal population.

stories.title: "Charlie’s assassination wasn’t even about him": Candace Owens sparks outrage with explosive new Charlie Kirk assassination claim
stories.summary: Candace Owens is facing fresh backlash after making new claims about Charlie Kirk's death, suggesting he may have been killed after allegedly refusing to participate in a plot against her. A viral X post accused Owens of making the tragedy about herself and condemned her remarks. Her comments have fuelled intense online debate, with critics questioning the allegations and supporters continuing to defend her.

stories.title: India welcomes Canada's remark delinking government from Nijjar killing
Middle East crisis: Government lodges protest with Iran as sailor dies in fresh attacks
stories.summary: India summoned Iran's deputy chief of mission to protest recent attacks on commercial ships. One Indian seafarer tragically lost his life and two others were critically injured. These attacks on vessels like MT Al Bahiyah and MT Mombasa have intensified recently. India strongly condemned the violence and urged an immediate cessation of hostilities. The government seeks the restoration of free and safe navigation through international waterways.

stories.title: On South China Sea, government backs tribunal ruling against Beijing
stories.summary: India supports freedom of navigation and lawful sea uses in the South China Sea. The Ministry of External Affairs responded to a joint statement by several nations. This statement rejected China's expansive South China Sea claim as lacking legal basis. It also reaffirmed a 2016 tribunal ruling favoring the Philippines. India emphasizes peaceful dispute resolution in accordance with UNCLOS principles.

stories.title: Give Muslims alternative site for namaz: Supreme Court to Dhar administration
stories.summary: The Supreme Court will hear challenges to a Madhya Pradesh High Court ruling on the Bhojshala complex. It declined to stay the order which declared the site a temple. Muslim petitioners argued the ruling ignored historical evidence and existing arrangements. The court directed authorities to find an alternative space for Friday prayers. Structural changes to the complex are prohibited without court permission.

stories.title: Passport just a document to regulate departure of citizens from India: MEA
stories.summary: The MEA clarified passport issuance follows the Passports Act, 1967. This document regulates departure of Indian citizens from India. Official sources state a passport is not a determinant of citizenship. Less than eight percent of Indians currently hold a passport. This clarification follows recent government official remarks on the travel document.

stories.title: Air India crash: Draft final report on Ahmedabad tragedy will be ready only by October, AAIB tells Supreme Court
stories.summary: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau informed the Supreme Court about the inquiry timeline. The complex investigation into the Air India crash is expected to conclude soon. Analysis activities will be completed within six weeks, subject to external factors. A draft final report is anticipated by October 2026 for review. This timeline aligns with international practices for accident investigations.

stories.title: Vietnam boat survivor: Captain jumped, so did I
stories.summary: A survivor described the sudden Vietnam boat tragedy where the captain jumped overboard. He explained that only those who followed him into the water managed to escape. The closed boat prevented rear passengers from exiting, leading to their demise. He lost a childhood friend in the unfortunate incident. Improved island medical access could have saved additional lives.

stories.title: Need to relook if English can be considered an indigenous language: Supreme Court
stories.summary: The Supreme Court questioned English's indigenous status while refusing to halt the CBSE's three-language scheme. This policy aims to promote Hindi and regional languages, aligning with constitutional goals. Petitioners argued against the scheme due to teacher and infrastructure challenges. They also noted limited availability of books on the NCERT website. The Centre and CBSE will file their responses within ten days.

stories.title: Staines' killer Dara Singh to be released soon?
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has set August 19 as a deadline for Odisha to decide on Dara Singh's remission plea. Dara Singh, jailed since 2000, is seeking release after serving over 26 years. The state sentence review board is favorably considering his plea due to good conduct. Updated information is required by the board before a final decision can be made.

stories.title: Hydel project near China border gets green clearance
stories.summary: An expert panel recommended green clearance for the Naying hydro-electric project. This project will be built across the Siyom river in Arunachal Pradesh. It will boost renewable energy generation and cost an estimated Rs 11,835 crore. The project proponent will provide compensation and rehabilitation for displaced families. Further forest clearance is now required for this significant development.

stories.title: Nitin Gadkari: Ethanol a small share of sons' business, attacks motivated
stories.summary: Union minister Nitin Gadkari denied personal gain from the ethanol blending program. He stated that allegations of conflict of interest are politically motivated and lack substance. Gadkari emphasized his long-standing support for alternative fuels to reduce pollution and import dependence. He clarified that his sons' business has a minimal share in the ethanol sector. The minister also highlighted the program's historical backing from previous governments.

stories.title: ‘Fake Silver’ row: Jammu court summons IO, seeks records
stories.summary: A Jammu court has ordered a crime branch officer to appear with case records. This follows objections raised over the agency's handling of a complaint. The case involves alleged fake silver offerings worth Rs 500 crore at Vaishno Devi shrine. Officials discovered the offerings contained minimal actual silver and toxic cadmium. An advocate filed a court complaint after his earlier submission received no action.

stories.title: 12 Gurgaon bikers, UP SUV driver fined Rs 1.7 lakh for off-roading in Ladakh’s protected areas
stories.summary: Twelve bikers from Gurgaon faced fines totaling Rs 1.2 lakh for off-roading near Tso Moriri. An SUV driver from Uttar Pradesh was also fined Rs 50,000 for a similar violation. These actions follow recent penalties against tourists for illegal incursions into protected areas. Wildlife officials are continuing their crackdown on off-roading in sensitive ecological zones. The administration urges tourists to explore Ladakh responsibly and protect its fragile environment.

stories.title: Jammu and Kashmir: CCTVs capture terror suspects, sparks search operation in Rajouri
stories.summary: Security forces initiated extensive searches in Rajouri's Thanamandi region after CCTV footage showed two terror suspects. These operations are part of an ongoing combing effort in the forested areas for elusive militants. Meanwhile, a drone was discovered by a local resident in Samba district's agricultural fields. The recovered drone was promptly seized by security personnel for forensic examination. Investigations are underway to determine the drone's origin and potential cross-border connections.

stories.title: NIA court issues non-bailable warrant for Hafiz Saeed; calls for crackdown on terror financing and networks
stories.summary: An NIA court has issued a non-bailable warrant for Hafiz Saeed. This action stems from the April 22, 2025, Pahalgam terror attack. The attack tragically resulted in the deaths of twenty-six innocent people. Saeed, the Lashkar-e-Taiba founder, is considered the mastermind of this conspiracy. stories.summary: Scientists have found GJ 3378b, a planet near Earth with potential for life. This exoplanet is twice Earth's size and orbits within its star's habitable zone. Researchers used ground-based instruments to update measurements of GJ 3378b's mass. Future telescopes will study its atmosphere to confirm habitability and search for biosignatures. This discovery adds GJ 3378b to the list of promising nearby exoplanets.

stories.summary: Oklahoma's "No Tolerance" signs remind drivers that posted speed limits are absolute. These signs reinforce the state's strict approach to speeding enforcement and traffic safety. stories.summary: Entering a new room can cause temporary memory lapses for your original intention. This doorway effect is a normal brain process for organizing experiences into distinct events. It happens as your brain updates its mental model of the environment. Working memory limitations and attention shifts also contribute to these forgetful moments. Retracing your steps often helps retrieve the forgotten thought by restoring context.

stories.title: NASA’s New Horizons travelled 3 billion miles over 9 years to reach Pluto – but it was moving too fast to stop when it arrived
stories.summary: NASA's New Horizons spacecraft completed its swift flyby of Pluto after a nine-year journey. The mission prioritized data collection over live communication during the brief encounter. Scientists received approximately 50 billion bits of data over fifteen months after the flyby. External affairs minister S Jaishankar highlighted the country's peacekeeping and development partnerships. India presented its SHANTI vision for global governance and cooperation among nations. The nation seeks support for its candidature amid a changing global landscape. India previously served eight terms as a non-permanent Security Council member.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Justin Trudeau: 'I don’t read the newspapers, I don’t watch the news. I figure, if something important happens, someone will tell me' and his detachment from politics
Supreme Court quashes Guwahati high court order on 27 'foreigners'
stories.summary: The Supreme Court stressed fair procedures for declaring individuals foreign nationals. It found fault with tribunals and the Guwahati High Court's actions. Many orders were quashed as they lacked hearings for affected people. The court directed tribunals to provide fresh hearings and reconsider cases. This ensures lawful adjudication and protects constitutional rights for all.

stories.title: Clavicular claims Israel Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's advisers suggested a gym livestream to reach younger voters
stories.summary: A streamer named Clavicular claims Netanyahu's advisers sought his help. They reportedly wanted a gym livestream to improve the leader's image. Clavicular stated advisers believed Netanyahu appeared old and out of shape. This claim remains unverified by any official confirmation. A meeting with an adviser was confirmed at a nightclub.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Dale Carnegie: "Don't be afraid of enemies who attack you. Be afraid of…" - why honest criticism is more valuable than praise
stories.summary: Dale Carnegie cautioned against trusting flattering friends more than open enemies. He argued that sincere criticism offers valuable lessons for personal growth. Flattery creates a false sense of security, hindering honest self-reflection. As influence grows, people often avoid challenging powerful individuals. Seeking truthful feedback remains crucial for lasting judgment and improvement.

stories.title: Jammu and Kashmir: 18 Amarnath yatris injured in Ramban multi-vehicle collision
stories.summary: Eighteen pilgrims sustained injuries in a multi-vehicle collision involving several buses and a car. The accident occurred on the Jammu-Srinagar National Highway in Ramban district early Monday. All injured pilgrims were promptly taken to the Ramban district hospital for treatment. They had sustained only minor injuries and were reported to be in stable condition. Police have initiated an investigation into the cause of the unfortunate pile-up.

stories.title: Colombian man with Social Security Number, work authorization killed by ICE agents in Maine: 'He was bleeding profusely from the head'
Jammu and Kashmir: BJP slaps Rs 100 crore notice on Omar over MLA poaching charge
stories.summary: The BJP has issued a Rs 100-crore defamation notice to Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah. This action follows Abdullah's allegations that a BJP functionary attempted to poach his party MLA. The notice demands an unconditional public apology from Abdullah within seven days. Abdullah dismissed the notice, viewing it as a sign of his political significance. He also warned of legal counter-notices against BJP functionaries for their past statements.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Marcus Aurelius: 'The only wealth which you will keep forever is the wealth...'
stories.summary: The philosophical musings of ancient Roman thinkers reveal that genuine wealth stems from the act of giving. Unlike material possessions, which fade over time, generosity fosters enduring character and deep social connections. This age-old wisdom stands in stark contrast to the practice of hoarding, which provides merely an illusion of security. Today, embracing generosity mirrors contemporary charitable endeavors and strategic investments, ultimately converting fleeting assets into lasting positive impact.

stories.title: ‘Democratic decentralisation’: Government announces hill councils for all 7 Ladakh districts
stories.summary: Ladakh will establish hill development councils in all seven districts to strengthen grassroots governance. This move aims to decentralize power and improve administrative reach across the vast territory. Currently, only Leh and Kargil districts have these autonomous district councils. Discussions are ongoing for a unique UT-level legislative body with broad powers. A draft framework for this new arrangement will be prepared soon.

stories.title: Quote of the Day by Napoleon Bonaparte: 'Never interrupt your enemy when he is making a mistake'
stories.summary: The concept of strategic patience can provide a significant edge in competitive environments. By letting rivals make their own missteps, one can capitalize on the ensuing turmoil. Historical figures like Napoleon Bonaparte utilized this method effectively at the Battle of Austerlitz. In contemporary business and political arenas, this approach highlights the importance of timing and self-restraint rather than hasty actions.

stories.title: Kai Cenat drops ‘EBK’ diss track targeting FunnyMike, DDG, Rakai and other Streamer University critics
stories.summary: Kai Cenat has released a diss track titled EBK, targeting creators who criticized his event. The song addresses complaints about the Streamer University 2026 selection process. FunnyMike and DDG were specifically called out in the new track. This online feud continues as the event approaches its scheduled start. Fans anticipate further responses from involved creators and critics.

stories.title: Early humans fed salmon to canines 12,000 years ago, that is why dogs are friendly companions
stories.summary: Recent findings reveal that ancient dogs in Alaska had a unique partnership with humans, dating back 12,000 years. This evidence indicates that these canines often shared salmon with early settlers, shedding light on the evolving dynamics between humans and dogs in the Americas. The analysis of fossilized bones uncovered a diet rich in fish, prompting a reevaluation of wolf domestication theories and illustrating a nuanced history of human-canine interactions.

stories.title: Quote of the day by former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe: "My opinion is that politicians should be humble in the face of history. And whenever history is a matter of debate, it…" - a thoughtful reflection reminds us that history deserves humility, evidence and careful scholarship, not political convenience
stories.summary: Shinzo Abe believed politicians should be humble regarding history. He stated that historians and experts should handle debated historical issues. Abe's own record on wartime conduct faced criticism from historians. This highlights a gap between his stated principle and actions. His words remind us that history requires careful scholarship, not political convenience.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Rishi Sunak: 'The greatest sacrifice I have made is that I have been an appalling husband and father for the past couple of years'
Jammu and Kashmir: Court remands 3 arrested publishers in police custody
stories.summary: Three publishers were remanded to police custody for ten days in Jammu. This case involves books with separatist content supplied to government school libraries. Sub-committees selected titles, but two books were later flagged for objectionable material. Over one hundred copies of each book had already reached schools before withdrawal. An inquiry was ordered, and eight education officials were suspended.

stories.title: Jammu & Kashmir administrtion seals Martyrs’ Graveyard; Omar, Mehbooba pay homage at party offices
stories.summary: Authorities restricted access to Srinagar's Martyrs' Graveyard on Monday. Political leaders paid homage at their respective party offices instead. Last year, Omar Abdullah bypassed barricades to reach the graveyard. The administration removed July 13 and December 5 from public holidays. This action followed the abrogation of Article 370 in January 2020.

stories.title: Jammu and Kashmir: CM Omar Abdullah’s Trump remarks anger BJP, party says it’s attempt to ‘internationalise Kashmir’
stories.summary: BJP criticized Omar Abdullah for invoking Donald Trump regarding Jammu and Kashmir statehood. Abdullah sarcastically suggested approaching Trump for statehood after BJP remarks. He also responded to a false tweet attributed to President Trump. BJP stated Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of India. They emphasized the central government's commitment to restoring statehood.

stories.title: Steve Jobs' widow Laurene grew up lower middle class, but now spends summers aboard superyacht
stories.summary: Laurene Powell Jobs navigated financial hardships during her childhood in rural New Jersey. She accumulated significant wealth through her investments in Apple and Disney after settling her student loans. Her first venture, Terravera, emphasized organic food and eco-friendly principles. While Apple faced initial economic challenges, it eventually soared in profitability. Today, the luxurious superyacht Venus stands as a testament to her extraordinary success.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Roger Federer: "I'm as patient a father as I am on the tennis court. It takes a lot for me to get really upset, but…"
stories.summary: Roger Federer admits parenting tests his renowned patience, which is usually seen on court. He acknowledges that children can indeed provoke frustration, even in calm individuals. This honest confession removes unrealistic expectations many parents place upon themselves. Patience involves responding with care even after frustration arises, not pretending it never happens. Federer's experience shows that professional success does not exempt anyone from ordinary family life.

stories.title: SAD chief Sukhbir Badal's close aide Dalvir Singh Kala shot at by bike-borne attacker in Punjab hospitalised
stories.summary: Shiromani Akali Dal leader Dalvir Singh Kala was shot and injured by an assailant. The incident occurred in Punjab's Mansa district on Monday evening. Kala, a former Zila Parishad member, was attacked near his shop. Police are investigating the shooting and examining CCTV footage. Efforts are underway to identify and apprehend the motorcycle-borne attacker.

stories.title: Zombie filler: Dead people's fat is the latest beauty trend
US judge scraps Trump's IRS settlement deal, says lawsuit sought to 'manipulate judicial process'
stories.summary: A federal judge voided President Trump's settlement with the IRS. The lawsuit was deemed an improper attempt to manipulate the judicial process. Sanctions and disciplinary actions were recommended against involved lawyers. The judge found the parties were not truly opposing each other. The Justice Department was criticized for its role in the settlement.

stories.title: Ex-Meta techie wraps up 14 years of life in US after layoff, says he's tired of immigration clock
Isro accomplishes 3 key qualification tests for crew module systems for Gaganyaan mission
'Mastermind was not happy': Louvre burglars reveal how they pulled off €88 million jewel heist
Bodies of 15 Indians killed in Vietnam boat tragedy arrive in Mumbai
stories.summary: The bodies of fifteen Indian nationals killed in Vietnam's boat tragedy have arrived in Mumbai. Ten victims were from Tamil Nadu, three from Andhra Pradesh, and two from Kerala. One Indian national remains hospitalized in Phu Quoc after a medical procedure. The speedboat carrying thirty-two Indian tourists capsized near Phu Quoc Island on Friday. Vietnamese authorities have ordered an investigation into the incident and detained the operator.

stories.title: Inside Christopher Plummer’s former Darien waterfront estate with a $12.995 million price tag
stories.summary: A historic Colonial estate from 1866, previously home to actor Christopher Plummer, has hit the market in Darien, Connecticut. This stunning waterfront property, boasting modern updates and direct access to a private sandy beach, exemplifies luxury coastal living. With a high-demand property market in Darien, interested buyers will need to act quickly to seize the opportunity.

stories.title: 'More destructive than US': China hits out at Japan's military role in South China Sea
'Intolerable threat to US sovereignty': Why Trump wants to 'dismantle' International Criminal Court
stories.summary: The Trump administration initiated a campaign against the International Criminal Court. This action targets the court's authority over American officials and military personnel. The United States argues the court threatens national sovereignty and self-governance. Diplomatic efforts and potential sanctions will be employed to disable the court. This move aims to protect American citizens from international prosecution.

stories.title: 'Will we just watch him succumb?' : Sonam Wangchuk's health worsens after 16 days of fast
Where are the Gandhi siblings? Why Wayanad landslide has put Rahul, Priyanka in the line of BJP fire
stories.summary: The BJP is raising eyebrows over Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi's absence from Wayanad following a landslide, labeling them as part-time politicians and political tourists. Wayanad is crucial for the Gandhis, as it has been a significant political stronghold for Rahul. Meanwhile, Rahul has not been seen publicly for almost three weeks. In response, Congress defends their leaders, stating their absence helps maintain the focus on relief operations.

stories.title: Ladakh: Autonomous Hill Councils for all seven districts
'King' Guramrit Sidhu sentenced to 20 years in prison in Los Angeles for US-Canada drug trafficking; spared from life sentence as lawyer says his offence was not violent
A US inmate demanded pasta in Tihar: What does a prison meal look like in different countries
stories.summary: A US citizen arrested in a terror case seeks court permission to cook his own food. He has been on a hunger strike for over 50 days due to prison food. Matthew Aaron VanDyke claims jail meals are unsuitable for his dietary habits. His family is willing to cover all expenses for his personal cooking setup. The court has sought a response from Tihar Jail authorities.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Muhammad Ali, "The Greatest": "I try not to speak about all the charities and people I help, because…" - a timeless lesson reveals that the purest acts of kindness are often the ones no one ever sees
stories.summary: Muhammad Ali believed true generosity requires no expectation of return. He deliberately avoided publicizing his extensive charitable work and humanitarian efforts. This approach highlighted his commitment to helping others without seeking personal recognition. The article emphasizes that quiet acts of kindness often carry the most significant impact. Ali's perspective remains relevant in today's highly visible world.

stories.title: 'Your prayers, efforts gave us strength': Indian Embassy thanks Vietnam as bodies of boat tragedy victims return home
stories.summary: The mortal remains of fifteen Indian tourists who died in Vietnam have arrived in Mumbai. State governments will coordinate the transportation of bodies to their final destinations. Vietnamese authorities and citizens provided significant support following the tragic boat accident. Sixteen rescued Indian tourists have already returned to India safely. One injured Indian national remains hospitalized in Ho Chi Minh City.

stories.title: This supersonic jet needed a radiation meter because it flew twice as high as commercial aircraft
stories.summary: The Concorde jet soared near the edge of space, requiring careful monitoring of radiation levels to ensure passenger safety. In the face of hazardous cosmic storms, pilots were mandated to descend to safer altitudes. While this supersonic aircraft typically flew above the majority of Earth's atmospheric shield, fluctuations in radiation exposure depended on several factors including altitude, geography, and solar activity. During such storms, safety took precedence over speed.

stories.title: Scientists say crushing deep-ocean pressure squeezes hidden nutrients out of sinking marine snow, feeding microbes and changing what we know about Earth’s carbon cycle
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that the immense pressure in the deep ocean squeezes nutrients out of sinking marine snow—tiny particles of dead algae and organic matter—providing an unexpected food source for deep-sea microbes. The findings suggest more carbon escapes into deep ocean water than previously believed, which could reshape scientists' understanding of Earth's carbon cycle and improve future climate models.

stories.title: Poland's 300-year-old 'Vampire Cemetery' mystery: The strange reason 100 people were buried with sickles, locks and unusual rituals
Britain bought 1,525 acres nearly lifeless farmland, now beavers are helping it make money
stories.summary: A farm in Lincolnshire is evolving into a lucrative wildland endeavor, with beavers playing a pivotal role in this ecological project. The initiative focuses on demonstrating that restoring nature can lead to substantial private income. Current revenue streams are generated through carbon removal and biodiversity credits, with aspirations to draw significant investments for sustainable environmental solutions.

stories.title: When will life on Earth come to an end? Scientists have finally found the doomsday date
stories.summary: Earth's plant life may persist for approximately 1.8 billion more years. The Sun's increasing brightness will gradually make conditions too harsh for vegetation. Hardy plant species adapted to extreme conditions will likely be the last survivors. This slow fading of life contrasts with dramatic disaster movie endings. The planet's eventual uninhabitability will unfold over an immense stretch of time.

stories.title: UK bans Iran Revolutionary Guards, blames IRGC-backed group for attacks on Jews
Army seeks to add organic pulses to troops’ diet
stories.summary: The Indian Army has requested organic pulses for its personnel, initiating a pilot program. Government cooperatives Nafed and NCCF will identify sources and manage the supply chain. This move aims to encourage farmers to produce organic pulses with assured demand. Organic pulses offer health benefits and require careful handling and certification. The pilot program will establish an institutional requirement for sustainable nutrition within the force.

stories.title: A supernova lit up Earth’s sky in 1054 and was visible in daylight. Hubble now shows its glowing remains are still expanding nearly 1,000 years later
stories.summary: Astronomers used the Hubble Space Telescope to measure the expanding Crab Nebula. New images compared with older ones show gas filaments moving outwards. This ancient stellar explosion's remnant is still actively changing today. The Crab Pulsar at the center continues to power the nebula's glow. Scientists also identified previously unrecognised filament structures within the nebula.

stories.title: H-1B techie, stuck in India for 18 months, sues officials for delay in visa; court dismisses, says it's not unreasonable
How Israel's Mossad tried to recruit Iran's former president Ahmadinejad; what happened next
stories.summary: Israel's Mossad reportedly sought to recruit Mahmoud Ahmadinejad for regime change. Secret meetings and financial aid were allegedly provided to the former Iranian president. An attempted extraction from Tehran failed after Ahmadinejad grew dissatisfied with the plan. Iranian authorities later placed Ahmadinejad under house arrest after uncovering his alleged contacts. No official confirmations have been issued by either involved nation.

stories.title: Six of seven cyber threats flagged last year now operational: BFSI report
5 lakes with underwater forests: From Clear Lake to Caddo Lake
Scottish man dies after two 999 calls fail to send ambulance
stories.summary: Brian Hurton tragically passed away after making two emergency calls that went completely unanswered. During his desperate wait for assistance, he was instructed to remain on the line, battling for breath. Shockingly, the ambulance didn't arrive until over three hours after his initial call. Paramedics found him dead upon their eventual arrival, prompting an investigation that uncovered flaws in the call response process and highlighted a failure to prioritize appropriately.

stories.title: 2020 Delhi riots: Court convicts former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain in IB officer Ankit Sharma murder case
stories.summary: A Delhi court convicted former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and others for murder. The court found Hussain guilty of murder and rioting charges related to the 2020 riots. Nazim, Kashim, Anas, and Javed were also convicted for murder and other offenses. The court acquitted six other individuals accused in the case. Arguments on the quantum of sentence will be heard later.

stories.title: Why New Zealand forests look like a galaxy filled with glowworms at night
She moved from Los Angeles to San Francisco for an AI job. The biggest difference wasn't the technology
stories.summary: A journalist moved from Los Angeles to San Francisco for an AI startup role. She found a work culture focused on building products and new technology. Her journalism skills proved valuable in explaining complex AI concepts to a wider audience. While missing her home, she embraced this significant technological shift. She is grateful for the unexpected opportunity which changed her career path.

stories.title: MacKenzie Scott is still worth $33 billion after giving away $10 million a day for seven years
stories.summary: MacKenzie Scott, a prominent philanthropist, skillfully balances her substantial wealth with a commitment to giving away billions each year. Having endured financial struggles in her youth through low-wage jobs, her life changed dramatically post-divorce from Jeff Bezos when she gained valuable Amazon shares. Scott's unique approach involves providing unrestricted grants to organizations, a strategy that, while criticized by some tech moguls, far surpasses their charitable efforts.

stories.title: Every autumn, an ordinary Oregon forest suddenly starts smiling after foresters in 2011 planted western larch trees in a secret pattern among thousands of Douglas firs
'Can't ignore me': Omar Abdullah's 'love letter' jibe at BJP over Rs 100 crore legal notice
South Korean sailor found dead near border after North Korea ignored search request
Mitch McConnell issues proof he's alive in a photo from hospital, Internet says release a video to prove photo is not AI-generated
India excavated a 28 km artificial lake in the Thar Desert to line it with a plastic sheet: Aims to supply water to 5 million people in Jaisalmer and Barmer
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking initiative, Rajasthan has constructed an expansive artificial lake designed to augment water supply, benefitting around five million residents in Jaisalmer and Barmer. Lined with plastic to mitigate evaporation, this reservoir aims to maintain water supply during canal repairs. The grand opening of this essential water project is anticipated for July 2026.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Snoop Dogg: ‘You can take your boy out the hood but you can't take the hood out the homie’
stories.summary: The influence of our surroundings extends far beyond mere memories, deeply embedding in our character and daily behaviors. Our formative settings mold not only our speech and desires but also our fundamental instincts. Even as we advance in life, these early lessons remain pivotal, guiding our perceptions and interactions. This ongoing relationship underscores the importance of integrating past experiences as we navigate new paths in life.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: Strikes in Yemen, Iran; Mamata alleges EC bias & more
stories.summary: Strikes in Yemen and Iran have heightened regional tensions and caused casualties. Mamata Banerjee accused the Election Commission of favoring a rival Trinamool Congress faction. India is seeking better terms in US trade talks, though the government denies stalled negotiations. A Kerala man convicted in a double murder case showed no remorse in court. China's reported chipmaking breakthrough could reshape the global semiconductor race.

stories.title: 'Get ready for sudden death': Iran media's Lindsey Graham reference in warning to Trump, Netanyahu
stories.summary: Iranian newspapers featured Senator Lindsey Graham's death on their front pages. Some publications issued veiled warnings directed at the US and its leaders. One newspaper described Graham as the "Merchant of Death" following his sudden illness. State media celebrated his passing, calling him "sent to hell." These remarks fueled speculation among some supporters of President Trump's movement.

stories.title: Archaeologists uncover 3,000-year-old tomb near Egypt's Luxor; inscriptions suggest it belonged to a man named Paser from the Ramesside period
stories.summary: A 3,000-year-old tomb near Luxor has been discovered by archaeologists. This tomb is believed to belong to a senior official named Paser. Inscriptions within the tomb reveal his prestigious titles and administrative roles. The structure offers insights into ancient burial customs and beliefs about the afterlife. Further exploration promises more details about Paser and ancient Thebes.

From 'Islamic Republic of Japan' to 'Leon' Musk: List of Trump's latest verbal mix-ups
'Real' TMC row: Mamata Banerjee cries foul over EC's 'stoic silence', opposes more time for rebel camp
stories.summary: Mamata Banerjee asked the Election Commission to stop granting more time to the Ritabrata Banerjee faction. She alleged the poll body's silence gave the rebel group additional leeway. The rival faction claimed to be the real Trinamool Congress party. Mamata's camp argued its organizational committees remain valid until 2027. The Election Commission had previously set deadlines for both groups.

'Power to you Sonam and young cockroaches': Atishi joins CJP protest on day 24 as Wangchuk's health worsens
Could the 'Hobbit' human species still exist? New theory revives debate over Homo floresiensis
stories.summary: A strange theory suggests a human-like species, Homo floresiensis, may still inhabit Flores Island caves. These small-bodied hominins, known as Hobbits, were discovered in 2004 and puzzled scientists. Fossils indicate they lived recently, sharing the planet with early modern humans. While local knowledge hints at survival, scientists require physical evidence for confirmation. Most experts remain skeptical due to a lack of verifiable proof for living Hobbits.

stories.title: Russia's cyberwar on Europe: UK, EU strike back with joint sanctions, summon Kremlin's envoys
This AI founder walked away from a $300,000 life in San Francisco: 'No money could make me stay here'
stories.summary: Koby Conrad, founder of AI sobriety companion Sunflower, relocated to Buenos Aires. He found a better environment for building a family and his company. Conrad enjoys the city's culture, food, and significantly lower living costs. He feels more focused and productive away from San Francisco's tech-centric atmosphere. The move supports his desire to balance ambitious work with raising a family.

stories.title: In 1906, one wrong turn sent the SS Valencia into the Pacific's “Graveyard of the Pacific”, where more than 100 people died
Meet Victoria Gowramma: Indian princess who grew up inside Buckingham Palace and became the first royal to convert to Christianity, had Queen Victoria as her godmother
stories.summary: The tale of Princess Gowramma, daughter of the last Raja of Kodagu, begins with her baptism in London, where Queen Victoria assumed the role of her godmother and named her Victoria Gowramma. After marrying Colonel John Campbell and having a daughter, she encountered societal bias due to her appearance. Tragically, Princess Victoria Gowramma passed away from tuberculosis, her remarkable story fading into obscurity over time.

stories.title: 18 ancient Egyptian tombs found with golden tongues
stories.summary: Recently, a remarkable discovery was made with the unearthing of eighteen ancient Egyptian tombs near Marina el-Alamein. Among the intriguing artifacts found were sealed stone slabs, an impressive granite coffin, and dozens of gold tongues strategically placed in the mouths of mummies to assist them in speaking in the afterlife. Additionally, an intricately designed offering altar and a statue of Aphrodite were also uncovered, shedding light on ancient burial practices.

stories.title: Ayodhya Ram Mandir Trust opens applications for CEO post amid donation row, sets July 18 as deadline
stories.summary: The Ram Temple Trust is actively seeking a chief executive officer to oversee temple management. Interested candidates must submit their applications by July 18 for this key leadership position. This recruitment initiative unfolds under the Supreme Court’s investigation into alleged misappropriation of donations. The appointed CEO will be responsible for daily operations and will be based in Ayodhya, with the selection process anticipated to wrap up in the coming month.

stories.title: 'People's mandate cannot be defeated': Kerala HC orders oath ceremony for detained BJP councillor inside prison
65-year-old grandfather attacked by a Yellowstone bison was cracking jokes despite breaking multiple bones
Quote of the day by Winston Churchill: "Personally, I'm always ready to learn, although I do not…" - know why real learning often begins when comfort ends
stories.summary: Winston Churchill's famous quote highlights the human preference for learning over being taught. He acknowledged the discomfort of admitting gaps in one's own understanding. True growth requires embracing correction, even when it feels unpleasant. Curiosity and humility are essential partners for continuous improvement. This timeless wisdom remains relevant in today's information-rich world.

stories.title: A hidden cave in Norway protected a 75,000-year-old Arctic world until scientists finally uncovered it
Richard Feynman's unsent love letter to his late wife shows that love doesn't always end with goodbye

Why Prince George wore suit at Wimbledon, even in the heat
stories.summary: Prince George and Prince William attended the Wimbledon men's final in formal attire. They adhered to the Royal Box dress code, which mandates suits and ties. Despite the heat, this strict protocol was followed by the royal attendees. Children are rarely permitted in the exclusive Royal Box seating area. However, Prince George and Princess Charlotte were exceptions to this unwritten rule.

stories.title: Bengal's anti-goonda law comes into force: What it allows and why the oppn is worried
stories.summary: The Act empowers the BJP government with sweeping powers including preventive detention, property confiscation and the removal of suspected troublemakers from specific areas. The government says the law is aimed at tackling organised crime and anti-social activities, while the Opposition has criticised it as draconian and vulnerable to misuse. The government says the legislation is designed to strengthen public safety.
